akhfash:4-4.t: He said ﴿إِن تَتُوبَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا﴾: He made it (قلوب, "hearts") plural because they are two out of two. «[Translator's note: i.e., one heart belonging to each of two persons; such a pair is expressed with the plural.]»

akhfash:12-12.t: And He said ﴿وَمَرْيَمَ ٱبْنَةَ عِمْرَانَ﴾ and ﴿ٱمْرَأَةَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ on the construction: "And Allah set forth the wife of Pharaoh and Mary as an example" (وَضَرَبَ اللهُ امْرَأَةَ فِرْعَونَ وَمَرْيَمَ مَثَلا).

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكَ﴾ of your slave-woman Māriya the Copt, when he had relations with her in the house of Ḥafṣa while she was absent; she came and it distressed her that this had been in her house and on her bed — whereupon you said, "She is forbidden to me" — ﴿تَبْتَغِي﴾ by forbidding her ﴿مَرْضَاتَ أَزْوَاجِكَ﴾, i.e. their pleasure? ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾: He has forgiven you this forbidding.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿قَدْ فَرَضَ اللَّهُ﴾ has prescribed ﴿لَكُمْ تَحِلَّةَ أَيْمَانِكُمْ﴾ their dissolution by the expiation mentioned in Sūrat al-Māʾida; and among oaths is the forbidding of a slave-woman. Did he ﷺ make expiation? Muqātil said: he freed a slave for the forbidding of Māriya; and al-Ḥasan said: he did not make expiation, because he ﷺ is forgiven. ﴿وَاللَّهُ مَوْلَاكُمْ﴾ your Helper, ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَ﴾ mention ﴿إِذْ أَسَرَّ النَّبِيُّ إِلَى بَعْضِ أَزْوَاجِهِ﴾ — she is Ḥafṣa — ﴿حَدِيثًا﴾: it is the forbidding of Māriya, and he said to her, "Do not divulge it." ﴿فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَتْ بِهِ﴾ ʿĀʾisha, thinking there was no harm in that, ﴿وَأَظْهَرَهُ اللَّهُ﴾ He informed him ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ of what had been told, ﴿عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ﴾ to Ḥafṣa ﴿وَأَعْرَضَ عَنْ بَعْضٍ﴾ out of generosity on his part. ﴿فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَهَا بِهِ قَالَتْ مَنْ أَنْبَأَكَ هَذَا قَالَ نَبَّأَنِيَ الْعَلِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ﴾, i.e. Allah.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿إِنْ تَتُوبَا﴾, i.e. Ḥafṣa and ʿĀʾisha, ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا﴾ have inclined towards the forbidding of Māriya, i.e. that pleased you both despite the Prophet's ﷺ dislike of it, and that is a sin — and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. you will be accepted. قُلُوبٌ (plural) is used for two hearts, and the dual was not used for it because combining two duals in what is like a single word is felt to be heavy. ﴿وَإِنْ تَظَّاهَرَا﴾ — with assimilation of the second tāʾ, originally, into the ẓāʾ, and in a reading [تَظَاهَرَا] without it — you help one another ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾, i.e. against the Prophet, in what he dislikes, ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ﴾ — a separating pronoun (faṣl) — ﴿مَوْلَاهُ﴾ his Helper, ﴿وَجِبْرِيلُ وَصَالِحُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both — conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the position of the ism of إِنَّ, so they are his helpers — ﴿وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ﴾ after the help of Allah and those mentioned ﴿ظَهِيرٌ﴾ backers, helpers for him in his support against you both.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿عَسَى رَبُّهُ إِنْ طَلَّقَكُنَّ﴾, i.e. if the Prophet divorced his wives, ﴿أَنْ يُبَدِّلَهُ﴾, with tashdīd and without it [يُبْدِلَهُ], ﴿أَزْوَاجًا خَيْرًا مِنْكُنَّ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of عَسَى, and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the replacement did not occur because the condition did not occur. ﴿مُسْلِمَاتٍ﴾ professing Islam, ﴿مُؤْمِنَاتٍ﴾ sincere, ﴿قَانِتَاتٍ﴾ obedient, ﴿تَائِبَاتٍ عَابِدَاتٍ سَائِحَاتٍ﴾ fasting, or emigrating, ﴿ثَيِّبَاتٍ وَأَبْكَارًا﴾

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ﴾ by holding them to obedience to Allah ﴿نَارًا وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ﴾ the disbelievers ﴿وَالْحِجَارَةُ﴾ such as their idols made from them; meaning that it is excessively hot, kindled by what is mentioned, not like the fire of this world which is kindled by firewood and the like; ﴿عَلَيْهَا مَلَائِكَةٌ﴾ its keepers, whose number is nineteen, as will come in al-Muddaththir, ﴿غِلَاظٌ﴾ from harshness of heart, ﴿شِدَادٌ﴾ in seizing, ﴿لَا يَعْصُونَ اللَّهَ مَا أَمَرَهُمْ﴾: a badal (substitute) from the Name of Majesty, i.e. they do not disobey the command of Allah, ﴿وَيَفْعَلُونَ مَا يُؤْمَرُونَ﴾: emphasis (taʾkīd). The verse is a warning to the believers against apostasy, and to the hypocrites who believe with their tongues and not their hearts.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَا تَعْتَذِرُوا الْيَوْمَ﴾: that will be said to them on their entering the Fire, i.e. because it will not benefit you; ﴿إِنَّمَا تُجْزَوْنَ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾, i.e. its recompense.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا تُوبُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ تَوْبَةً نَصُوحًا﴾, with fatḥa on the nūn and with ḍamma: sincere, in that one does not return to the sin nor intend to return to it. ﴿عَسَى رَبُّكُمْ﴾: an expression of hope that will come to pass, ﴿أَنْ يُكَفِّرَ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ﴾ gardens ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ يَوْمَ لَا يُخْزِي اللَّهُ﴾ by entry into the Fire ﴿النَّبِيَّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ نُورُهُمْ يَسْعَى بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ in front of them ﴿وَ﴾ it will be ﴿بِأَيْمَانِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ﴾ — resumptive (mustaʾnaf) — ﴿رَبَّنَا أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا﴾ to Paradise, while the hypocrites' light is extinguished, ﴿وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا﴾, our Lord; ﴿إِنَّكَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ جَاهِدِ الْكُفَّارَ﴾ with the sword ﴿وَالْمُنَافِقِينَ﴾ with the tongue and proof, ﴿وَاغْلُظْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ with rebuke and loathing; ﴿وَمَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ is it.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا امْرَأَتَ نُوحٍ وَامْرَأَتَ لُوطٍ كَانَتَا تَحْتَ عَبْدَيْنِ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا صَالِحَيْنِ فَخَانَتَاهُمَا﴾ in religion, since they both disbelieved. The wife of Noah, whose name was Wāhila, used to tell his people that he was mad; and the wife of Lot, whose name was Wāʿila, used to direct his people to his guests when they stayed with him, by night by lighting a fire and by day by making smoke. ﴿فَلَمْ يُغْنِيَا﴾, i.e. Noah and Lot, ﴿عَنْهُمَا مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ from His punishment ﴿شَيْئًا وَقِيلَ﴾ to them both: ﴿ادْخُلَا النَّارَ مَعَ الدَّاخِلِينَ﴾ of the disbelievers of the people of Noah and the people of Lot.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا امْرَأَتَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾: she believed in Moses, and her name was Āsiya; Pharaoh tortured her by staking down her hands and feet, putting a huge millstone on her chest and exposing her to the sun; and whenever those charged with her dispersed from her, the angels shaded her. ﴿إِذْ قَالَتْ﴾ in the state of torture: ﴿رَبِّ ابْنِ لِي عِنْدَكَ بَيْتًا فِي الْجَنَّةِ﴾ — it was unveiled to her and she saw it, and the torture became easy for her — ﴿وَنَجِّنِي مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ وَعَمَلِهِ﴾ and his torture, ﴿وَنَجِّنِي مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the people of his religion. So Allah took her soul. Ibn Kaysān said: she was raised to Paradise alive, and she eats and drinks.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَمَرْيَمَ﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to امْرَأَةِ فِرْعَوْنَ; ﴿ابْنَتَ عِمْرَانَ الَّتِي أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا﴾ guarded it, ﴿فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهِ مِنْ رُوحِنَا﴾, i.e. Gabriel, when he blew into the opening of her shift, through Allah the Exalted creating his act reaching her private part, and she conceived Jesus; ﴿وَصَدَّقَتْ بِكَلِمَاتِ رَبِّهَا﴾ His laws ﴿وَكُتُبِهِ﴾ the revealed ones, ﴿وَكَانَتْ مِنَ الْقَانِتِينَ﴾ of the obedient people.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ «يا» is a vocative particle, and the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), and «ها» is for drawing attention (tanbīh); ﴿النَّبِيُّ﴾ a badal (substitute) for «أيّها»; ﴿لِمَ﴾ the lām is a preposition, and «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of a genitive (majrūr) governed by the lām, and both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb after them; ﴿تُحَرِّمُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿لَكَ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿تَبْتَغِي مَرْضاتَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil being latent, and the clause is circumstantial (a ḥāl). ﴿أَزْواجِكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct). ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its two khabars (predicates), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿قَدْ فَرَضَ اللَّهُ﴾ «قد» is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq), and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿تَحِلَّةَ أَيْمانِكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), annexed (muḍāf), and «أيمانكم» is muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿اللَّهُ مَوْلاكُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿أَسَرَّ النَّبِيُّ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿إِلى بَعْضِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿أَزْواجِهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿حَدِيثاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; ﴿لما﴾ an adverb of time with conditional meaning, not making the verb jussive; ﴿نَبَّأَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); ﴿بِهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the clause is in the position of a genitive by iḍāfa; ﴿وَأَظْهَرَهُ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, the Name of Majesty being its fāʿil; ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿عَرَّفَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position; ﴿بَعْضَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَأَعْرَضَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «عرف»; ﴿عَنْ بَعْضٍ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; ﴿لما﴾ its i'rab has been given before; ﴿نَبَّأَها﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil being latent; ﴿بِهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the clause is in the position of a genitive by iḍāfa. ﴿قالَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position. ﴿مَنْ﴾ an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أَنْبَأَكَ﴾ a past verb and its first object, the fāʿil being latent; ﴿هذا﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, and the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of «من», and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿نَبَّأَنِيَ الْعَلِيمُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, «العليم» being its fāʿil; ﴿الْخَبِيرُ﴾ a naʿt (adjective), and the clause is the object of the saying.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿إِنْ تَتُوبا﴾ a conditional particle making the verb jussive, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, the alif being the fāʿil (agent); ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿فَقَدْ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of reason (taʿlīl); ﴿قد صَغَتْ﴾ a particle of realisation (taḥqīq) and a past verb; ﴿قُلُوبُكُما﴾ its fāʿil, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, and the clause «صغت» gives the reason, with no grammatical position; and the meaning of «صغت» is «مالت» (inclined). ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿إِنْ تَظاهَرا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «إن تتوبا», and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being «يجد ناصرا» (he will find a helper); ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ both are attached to the verb. ﴿فَإِنَّ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of reason; ﴿إن اللَّهِ﴾ «إنّ» and its noun «[Translator's note: the Name of Majesty is printed with a kasra in the source; in the verse it is «اللَّهَ», the accusative noun of «إنّ».]»; ﴿هُوَ﴾ a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿مَوْلاهُ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ», and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَجِبْرِيلُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿وَصالِحُ﴾ conjoined to «جبريل»; ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿وَالْمَلائِكَةُ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿بَعْدَ ذلِكَ﴾ an adverb of time annexed to the demonstrative; ﴿ظَهِيرٌ﴾ the khabar for what has preceded.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿عَسى﴾ a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb, one of the verbs of hope; ﴿رَبُّهُ﴾ its noun; ﴿إِنْ طَلَّقَكُنَّ﴾ «إن» is conditional and makes the verb jussive, and a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted; ﴿أَنْ يُبْدِلَهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by «أن», the hāʾ being the first object, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and what follows it is the khabar (predicate) of «عسى»; ﴿أَزْواجاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿خَيْراً﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «أزواجا»; ﴿مِنْكُنَّ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خيرا»; ﴿مُسْلِماتٍ، مُؤْمِناتٍ، قانِتاتٍ، تائِباتٍ، عابِداتٍ، سائِحاتٍ، ثَيِّباتٍ﴾ multiple naʿts of «أزواجا»; ﴿وَأَبْكاراً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ﴾ its i'rab has been given before; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the vocative clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿قُوا﴾ an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw being its fāʿil; ﴿أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وَأَهْلِيكُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «أنفسكم»; ﴿ناراً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «نارا»; ﴿وَالْحِجارَةُ﴾ conjoined to «الناس»; ﴿عَلَيْها﴾ a fronted khabar; ﴿مَلائِكَةٌ﴾ a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is a second naʿt of «نارا»; ﴿غِلاظٌ شِدادٌ﴾ two naʿts of «ملائكة»; ﴿لا﴾ negating; ﴿يَعْصُونَ اللَّهَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil and the Name of Majesty its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿ما﴾ a badal (substitute) for the Name of Majesty, and the clause is a third naʿt; ﴿أَمَرَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَيَفْعَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿يُؤْمَرُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is the ṣila of «ما».

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ﴾ its i'rab has been given before; ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين»; ﴿لا تَعْتَذِرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive «لا», the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is the object of an omitted saying (maqūl qawl maḥdhūf). ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿إِنَّما﴾ the restraining [«ما»] and the restrained [«إنّ»] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); ﴿تُجْزَوْنَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿ما﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ «كان» and its noun, and the clause is the ṣila; ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «كنتم».

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: its i'rab has been given before; ﴿تُوبُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿تَوْبَةً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿نَصُوحاً﴾ a naʿt (adjective); ﴿عَسى﴾ a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb; ﴿رَبُّكُمْ﴾ the noun of «عسى»; ﴿أَنْ يُكَفِّرَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by «أن», and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) made from «أن» and the verb is in the position of an accusative as the khabar (predicate) of «عسى»; ﴿عَنْكُمْ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿سَيِّئاتِكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its first object, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir), and the clause is conjoined to «يكفر»; ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb; ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ fāʿil, and the clause is a naʿt of «جنات»; ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿لا﴾ negating; ﴿يُخْزِي اللَّهُ النَّبِيَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «النبي»; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مَعَهُ﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿نُورُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يَسْعى﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ an adverb of place annexed to «أيديهم»; ﴿وَبِأَيْمانِهِمْ﴾ both are conjoined to the adverb; ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is a ḥāl; ﴿رَبَّنا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf); ﴿أَتْمِمْ﴾ a verb of supplication whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿لَنا﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿نُورَنا﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the two clauses are the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿وَاغْفِرْ لَنا﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّكَ﴾ «إنّ» and its noun; ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ both are attached to «قدير»; ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿قَدِيرٌ﴾ the khabar of «إنّ», and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya).

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ﴾ its i'rab has been given before. ﴿جاهِدِ الْكُفَّارَ﴾ an imperative verb, «الكفار» being its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وَالْمُنافِقِينَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الكفار»; ﴿وَاغْلُظْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَمَأْواهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is circumstantial (a ḥāl); ﴿وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿امْرَأَتَ نُوحٍ﴾ a badal (substitute), annexed to «نوح»; ﴿وَامْرَأَتَ لُوطٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿كانَتا﴾ «كان» and its noun; ﴿تَحْتَ﴾ an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of «كان»; ﴿عَبْدَيْنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿مِنْ﴾ ﴿عِبادِنا﴾ both are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «عبدين»; ﴿صالِحَيْنِ﴾ a naʿt of «عبدين», and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَخانَتاهُما﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَلَمْ يُغْنِيا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by «لم», the alif being its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿عَنْهُما﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ ḥāl; ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَقِيلَ﴾ a passive past verb, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿ادْخُلَا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿النَّارَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿مَعَ﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿الدَّاخِلِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا امْرَأَتَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾: the i'rab of its like has been given before. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿قالَتْ رَبِّ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the yāʾ of the first person, which has been dropped; ﴿ابْنِ﴾ a verb of supplication, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, the fāʿil being latent, and the two clauses are the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause «قالت» is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by being the second term of a genitive construct (iḍāfa); ﴿لِي﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ابن»; ﴿عِنْدَكَ﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿بَيْتاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿فِي الْجَنَّةِ﴾ both are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective); ﴿وَنَجِّنِي﴾ a verb of supplication and its mafʿūl bihi, the fāʿil being latent; ﴿مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ both are attached to the verb, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَعَمَلِهِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; ﴿وَنَجِّنِي مِنَ الْقَوْمِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ a naʿt of «القوم».

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَمَرْيَمَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «امرأة فرعون»; ﴿ابْنَتَ عِمْرانَ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of «مريم», annexed to «عمران»; ﴿الَّتِي﴾ also a naʿt of «مريم»; ﴿أَحْصَنَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿فَرْجَها﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فَنَفَخْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فِيهِ﴾ both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿مِنْ رُوحِنا﴾ both are attached to the verb as well. ﴿وَصَدَّقَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿بِكَلِماتِ﴾ both are attached to the verb; ﴿رَبِّها﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct); ﴿وَكُتُبِهِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَكانَتْ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent; ﴿مِنَ الْقانِتِينَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of «كانت», and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

dervis-irab:1-5.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَحِلَّةَ) a maṣdar (verbal noun) of حلّل with doubled [middle radical], like تكرمة; these two are not according to rule, for the regular maṣdar of [the pattern faʿʿala], when it is sound and without hamza [, is al-tafʿīl] [Translator's note: the source sentence is incomplete; the bracketed completion follows the evident sense]. As for the one whose final radical is weak, like زكّى, and the one whose final radical is hamza, like نبّأ, their maṣdars are تزكية and تنبئة; although al-tafʿīl has come in full in the weak verb, as in:
باتت تنزي دلوها تنزيا ... كما تنزي شهلة صبيا
(She spent the night jerking her bucket up and down, as an old woman jerks a child up and down.)
Its origin is تحللة, like تكرمة, and then [the two lāms] were assimilated.
(تَظاهَرا) with the second tāʾ of the original assimilated into the ẓāʾ, and in one reading without it [i.e. تظاهرا with lightening]; that is, "the two of you support one another".
(قانِتاتٍ) obedient.
(ثَيِّباتٍ) plural of ثيّب, from ثاب يثوب, i.e. he returned, as if she has returned [to her former state] after the loss of her virginity. Its origin is ثيوب, like سيّد and ميّت, whose origins are سيود and ميوت, and they underwent the phonetic change (iʿlāl) that will come in the section on benefits [Translator's note: so in the source; the section on benefits of this entry does not in fact treat it].

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ ما أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكَ تَبْتَغِي مَرْضاتَ أَزْواجِكَ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) The i'rab of يا أيها النبي has been given many times. As for لم: the lām is a preposition and ما is an interrogative noun in the position of genitive by the lām; it has been mentioned before that when a preposition enters upon the interrogative ما its alif is dropped. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) تحرم; ما is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause أحلّ الله is the ṣila (relative clause); لك is attached to أحلّ. The clause تبتغي is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of تحرم, and مرضاة أزواجك is the mafʿūl bihi. الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), غفور the khabar (predicate) and رحيم a second khabar.
(قَدْ فَرَضَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ تَحِلَّةَ أَيْمانِكُمْ) قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); فرض الله is a verb and its fāʿil; لكم is attached to فرض; تحلّة is the mafʿūl bihi and أيمانكم muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), i.e. Allah has legislated for you the release from your oaths in the manner set out at length in the books of law.
(وَاللَّهُ مَوْلاكُمْ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ) The wāw is a conjunction; الله is a mubtadaʾ and مولاكم the khabar; هو is a mubtadaʾ, العليم a first khabar and الحكيم a second khabar.
(وَإِذْ أَسَرَّ النَّبِيُّ إِلى بَعْضِ أَزْواجِهِ حَدِيثاً) The wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); إذ is the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, i.e. "remember"; the clause أسرّ النبي is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it, and حديثا is the mafʿūl bihi.
(فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَتْ بِهِ وَأَظْهَرَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ وَأَعْرَضَ عَنْ بَعْضٍ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; لمّا is an adverb meaning "when", or a linking [particle] containing the sense of condition; the clause نبّأت is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. The basic rule for أنبأ, نبّأ, أخبر, خبّر and حدّث is that they take one object by themselves and a second by means of a preposition, which may be omitted. So you say نبّأت به, the first object being omitted, i.e. "someone other than her"; and من أنبأك هذا, i.e. بهذا; and he said نبّأني, i.e. نبّأني به or نبّأنيه. When they are made to include the sense of أعلم ("to inform"), they take three objects, as in the poet's saying:
نبئت زرعة والسفاهة كاسمها ... يهدي إليّ غرائب الأشعار
(I was informed that Zurʿa — and folly is as its name — is sending me strange poems.)
In the verse, نبّأت takes two objects, the first of which is omitted, and the second is genitive with the bāʾ, i.e. "she told it to someone other than her". As for وأظهره: the wāw is a conjunction; أظهره, i.e. He informed him, is a verb and a mafʿūl bihi, الله is the fāʿil, and عليه is attached to أظهره. The clause عرّف has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussivizing condition; بعضه is the mafʿūl bihi; أعرض is conjoined to عرّف, and عن بعض is attached to أعرض. The second object of عرّف is omitted, i.e. he made her know part of what she had done. In one reading it is عَرَفَ with the lightened form, i.e. he requited [it] with reproach and blame, as you say to someone who hurts you: لأعرفنّ لك ذلك, i.e. "I will certainly requite you".
(فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَها بِهِ قالَتْ مَنْ أَنْبَأَكَ هذا قالَ نَبَّأَنِيَ الْعَلِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; لمّا is temporal, meaning "when", or a linking [particle] containing the sense of condition in either case. نبّأها is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; the clause قالت has no grammatical position. من is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the clause أنبأك is the khabar; the kāf is a first object and هذا a second object. قال is a past verb, and the clause نبّأني العليم الخبير is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); العليم is the fāʿil of نبّأني and الخبير an adjective.
(إِنْ تَتُوبا إِلَى اللَّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُما) إن is conditional and تتوبا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the alif is the fāʿil, and إلى الله is attached to تتوبا. The apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "He will turn to you [in forgiveness]". The fāʾ is causal; قد is a particle of realisation; صغت, i.e. inclined, is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents; the tāʾ is the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine, and قلوبكما is the fāʿil of صغت.
(وَإِنْ تَظاهَرا عَلَيْهِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ مَوْلاهُ وَجِبْرِيلُ وَصالِحُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction and إن is conditional; تظاهرا is the protasis, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the alif is the fāʿil, and عليه is attached to تظاهرا. The apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "he will find a helper". The fāʾ is causal; إنّ and its noun, هو is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), and مولاه is two khabars [Translator's note: so in the source, «خبران»; evidently for «خبرها» "its khabar"]; the pause is here. جبريل is a mubtadaʾ and صالح المؤمنين is conjoined to جبريل. صالح is a generic noun (ism jins), not a plural, and that is why it has come without a wāw after the ḥāʾ. They have permitted it to be a plural with wāw and nūn, the nūn being dropped for annexation, and written without the wāw in consideration of the pronunciation, since the wāw drops because of the meeting of two quiescents; but there is no need for this artificiality. You may also conjoin جبريل and صالح المؤمنين to the position of إنّ and its noun, so that the predicate of them all is مولاه; while on [the view of] its being a mubtadaʾ, the khabar is His saying ظهير, because in the pattern faʿīl the singular and the plural are the same, as has been mentioned before.
(وَالْمَلائِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ) You may conjoin الملائكة to what precedes, or parse it as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is ظهير; this has been pointed out already.
(عَسى رَبُّهُ إِنْ طَلَّقَكُنَّ أَنْ يُبْدِلَهُ أَزْواجاً خَيْراً مِنْكُنَّ) عسى is a past verb, one of the verbs of hope, and ربه is its noun. إن is conditional, and طلقكنّ is a past verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi, in the position of jussive as the protasis. أن is a maṣdar-forming and accusative particle; يبدله — with the lightened form, and it has also been read with doubling — is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن; أن and what falls within its scope are the khabar of عسى; the hāʾ is a first mafʿūl bihi. The apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then perhaps". أزواجا is a second mafʿūl bihi, خيرا an adjective, and منكنّ is attached to خيرا. The condition was placed between عسى and its khabar out of concern for the matter and to make them afraid.
(مُسْلِماتٍ مُؤْمِناتٍ قانِتاتٍ تائِباتٍ عابِداتٍ سائِحاتٍ ثَيِّباتٍ وَأَبْكاراً) مسلمات is a second naʿt (adjective) of أزواجا; it may also be parsed as a ḥāl, and some made it accusative by specification (ʿalā al-ikhtiṣāṣ), which is fine; what follows are multiple adjectives. The wāw was placed between ثيّبات and أبكارا because the two descriptions are mutually exclusive in this case, unlike the rest of the adjectives; it is not the "wāw of eight" (wāw al-thamāniya), as some have imagined. This has been discussed in detail before.

* Rhetoric:
He used the plural in His saying «قلوبكما», and this was permissible because it is annexed to a dual, namely the pronoun of the two of them. The plural in such a case is more frequently used than the dual; and the dual, [less] than the plural [Translator's note: the source's «والتثنية دون الجمع» "and the dual below the plural" evidently means the dual is less frequent than the plural], as the poet said:
فتخالسا نفسيهما بنوافذ ... كنوافذ العبط التي لا ترفع
(The two of them snatched each other's lives with piercing thrusts, like the piercing cuts in sound camels that are not mended.)
This was the regular rule, namely that a dual be expressed by a dual; but they disliked the combination of two duals, so they turned to the plural, because the dual is a plural in meaning. The singular is not permissible according to the Basrans except in poetry, as in:
حمامة بطن الواديين ترنمي ... سقاك من العز الفوادي مطيرها
(O dove of the hollow of the two valleys, coo! May the rainy one among the morning clouds water you.) [Translator's note: the source prints «العز الفوادي», evidently for «الغرّ الغوادي» "the white morning clouds".]
He means بطني ("the two hollows").

* Benefits:
The Messenger did not make the awe of prophethood a deterring barrier between himself and his wives; rather, by his gentleness and his friendliness he made them forget that they were addressing the Messenger of Allah, at certain times. So among them was one who would say to him in front of her father: "Speak, and say nothing but the truth"; and one who would argue back with him or be angry with him for the whole of her day; and one who reached a degree of boldness towards him that a man like ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, with his sternness, would hear of and marvel at, and he would be about to strike his daughter Ḥafṣa because she was bold as the other wives were bold. The following story is a true model of this sublime conduct. Most of the commentators said, in summary: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was alone with Māriya on ʿĀʾisha's day, and Ḥafṣa came to know of it, so he said to her: "Keep it secret; I have made Māriya unlawful for myself; and I give you the good news that Abū Bakr and ʿUmar will rule the affairs of my community after me." But she told ʿĀʾisha of it, and the two of them were close friends. It has also been said that he was alone with her on Ḥafṣa's day, and he placated her with that and asked her to keep it secret, but she did not keep it secret; so he divorced her and withdrew from his wives, and stayed twenty-nine nights in Māriya's house. It is related that ʿUmar said to her: "If there were any good in the family of al-Khaṭṭāb, he would not have divorced you." Then Jibrīl, upon him be peace, descended and said: "Take her back, for she fasts much and stands much in prayer, and she is one of your wives in the Garden."
It is also related that he drank honey in the house of Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, and ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa agreed together and said to him: "We smell on you the smell of maghāfīr." Maghāfīr is the plural of mughfūr, with ḍamma, like ʿuṣfūr: a sweet gum with an unpleasant smell, exuded by a tree called al-ʿurfuṭ (with ḍamma on the undotted ʿayn and on the fāʾ), found in the Ḥijāz, which has a smell like that of wine. He ﷺ disliked that an unpleasant smell should be found on him, so he made honey unlawful [for himself].
Al-Zamakhsharī was audacious and used, concerning the Prophet ﷺ, language that it is not permissible to use and that is not palatable to quote. Ibn al-Munayyir answered him with a sound reply and analysed this "making unlawful" with fine analysis. We confine ourselves to quoting it, passing over the remaining numerous views. Ibn al-Munayyir said:
«What al-Zamakhsharī said about the Prophet ﷺ is fabrication and slander, and the Prophet is free of it. That is because making unlawful what Allah has made lawful is of two kinds. [First:] believing that the ruling of unlawfulness is established for it; this is equivalent to believing the ruling of lawfulness for what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made unlawful, and both are forbidden and do not issue from those who bear the mark of faith; and if it did issue, it would strip the believer of the ruling and name of faith. The second: abstaining from what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made lawful; and taking "making unlawful" in its bare [sense] is correct, because of His saying "And We had forbidden to him the wet-nurses before", i.e. We prevented, nothing more. It may be reinforced by an oath while believing in its lawfulness, and this is purely permissible. The verse is to be taken according to the second kind, and the sound interpretation supports it: the Prophet ﷺ swore by Allah that he would not approach Māriya, and when the verse was revealed he made expiation for his oath; and what indicates it is: "Allah has ordained for you the release from your oaths". This degree is permissible, and there is no sin in doing it. It was said to him "Why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?" only out of gentleness towards him and compassion for him, and to exalt his standing and his rank ﷺ above having to consider the pleasure of his wives in what is hard on him, in accordance with what is familiar of Allah the Exalted's kindness to His Prophet and His raising him above being put out [Translator's note: the source prints «يخرج», evidently for «يحرج» "being put in difficulty"] on account of any of the human beings who are his followers and for whose sake they were created [Translator's note: so in the source; the intended sense is probably "for whose sake (i.e. the Prophet's) they were created"], so that Allah may show the perfection of his prophethood through the evidence of their falling short of him. Al-Zamakhsharī did not take "making unlawful" in this sense, because he made it a slip (zalla), and so takes it in the first sense. Allah forbid, and far be it from Allah! For even ordinary believers are far from believing unlawful what Allah has made lawful; so how could he not keep the rank of the Prophet above what even the rank of the common people of the community is raised above? This on al-Zamakhsharī's part is nothing but audacity towards Allah and His Messenger, speaking loosely without verification, and putting forward corrupt opinion without reflection».

dervis-irab:6-8.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ ناراً وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ وَالْحِجارَةُ) قوا is an imperative verb from al-wiqāya (protection), so its measure is عُوا, because the fāʾ [first radical] was dropped, as it occurs in the imperfect between a yāʾ and a kasra, and this [imperative] is modelled on that; and the lām [final radical] was dropped by analogy with the jussive. The explanation is that [the original is] أوقيوا [Translator's note: the source prints «أوقوا»; the full original form is أوقيوا], like اضربوا: the wāw, which is the fāʾ of the word, was dropped for the reason mentioned; the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) was dropped because the quiescent letter it introduced was dropped; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was found heavy and was dropped, so two quiescents met, and the yāʾ was dropped, and the letter before the wāw was given ḍamma so that it [the wāw] would be sound. The wāw is the fāʿil (agent), أنفسكم is a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and أهليكم is conjoined to أنفسكم, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural. نارا is a second mafʿūl bihi. وقودها is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and الناس the khabar (predicate), or the reverse; الحجارة is conjoined to النار [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently for «الناس»]. The clause وقودها الناس is an adjective of نارا.
(عَلَيْها مَلائِكَةٌ غِلاظٌ شِدادٌ لا يَعْصُونَ اللَّهَ ما أَمَرَهُمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ ما يُؤْمَرُونَ) The clause is a second adjective of نارا. عليها is a fronted khabar and ملائكة a postponed mubtadaʾ; غلاظ is a naʿt (adjective) of ملائكة and شداد a second naʿt. لا is negating; يعصون الله is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi. ما is maṣdariyya; أمرهم is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; ما with what it governs is interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar) in the position of accusative as a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from الله, as if it were said "they do not disobey His command". Abū Ḥayyān permitted its being accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "in what He commands them". As for ويفعلون: the wāw is a conjunction, and يفعلون is an imperfect verb, nominative, and its fāʿil; ما is a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause يؤمرون is the ṣila (relative clause), the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. "[commanded] with it". Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: are the two clauses not of one meaning? I answer: no; for the meaning of the first is that they accept His commands and hold to them, and the meaning of the second is that they carry out what they are commanded, without being sluggish about it or slack in it». So a difference is established. As for al-Bayḍāwī, he answered this question by saying: «It has been said: they do not disobey Allah in the past, and they do what they are commanded in the future».
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لا تَعْتَذِرُوا الْيَوْمَ إِنَّما تُجْزَوْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) لا is prohibitive; تعتذروا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا; اليوم is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) تعتذروا. The clause is the object of an omitted saying, i.e. that will be said to them upon entering the Fire. إنما is [إنّ] made inoperative by [ما] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); تجزون is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and ما is a second mafʿūl bihi; the clause كنتم is the ṣila of ما, and the clause تعملون is the khabar of كنتم.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا تُوبُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ تَوْبَةً نَصُوحاً) توبوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; إلى الله is attached to توبوا; توبة is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and نصوحا a naʿt of توبة.
(عَسى رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ يُكَفِّرَ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئاتِكُمْ) عسى is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb, one of the verbs of hope, and ربكم is its noun; أن and what falls within its scope are in the position of accusative as the khabar of عسى; عنكم is attached to يكفر, and سيئاتكم is the mafʿūl bihi.
(وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ) ويدخلكم is conjoined to يكفر; the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi and جنات a second mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause تجري is a naʿt of جنات; من تحتها is attached to تجري, and الأنهار is the fāʿil of تجري.
(يَوْمَ لا يُخْزِي اللَّهُ النَّبِيَّ) The adverb is attached to يدخلكم, or to an omitted verb whose implied form is "remember", in which case it would be a mafʿūl bihi. لا is negating; يخزي الله is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; النبي is the mafʿūl bihi.
(وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ نُورُهُمْ يَسْعى بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمانِهِمْ) The wāw may be a conjunction, with الذين in the position of accusative, conjoined in sequence to النبي; then نورهم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يسعى the khabar, and the clause is new (mustaʾnafa) or circumstantial. Or the wāw may be resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), with الذين a mubtadaʾ and the clause نورهم يسعى its khabar. As for بين أيديهم, the adverb is attached to يسعى, and بأيمانهم is conjoined to the adverb and attached to what it is attached to.
(يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا أَتْمِمْ لَنا نُورَنا) The clause is a second khabar or circumstantial. ربنا is a one addressed (munādā) in a genitive construct (muḍāf); the vocative clause, together with the imperative verb after it, its fāʿil and its object, is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
(وَاغْفِرْ لَنا إِنَّكَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) Conjoined to what precedes.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «توبة نصوحا» there is figurative attribution (isnād majāzī): sincerity is attributed to the repentance figuratively, whereas it really belongs to the one repenting, for hyperbole. Its like has preceded many times.
2- In His saying «لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون» there is a wonderful figure which they have called "negation and affirmation" (al-salb wa-l-ījāb). It is building speech upon negating a thing from one aspect and affirming it from another, or commanding a thing from one aspect and forbidding it from another aspect; it has been discussed before. In the verse it is clear: He, Mighty and Majestic, negated disobedience of these described beings and affirmed obedience for them. If it is said: on the apparent sense of this verse there is a difficulty in terms of overlap and repetition, for the meaning of its end is included in the meaning of its beginning, so it is repeated even though its wording differs, and this is a defect from which the composition of the Mighty Book is kept free, since whoever does not disobey obeys — I have not seen anyone address this difficulty and answer it except the Imām Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī, who said: «They do not disobey Allah in the present, and they do what they are commanded in the future»; and that is, in any case, an answer that does not resolve the difficulty, which rather remains. Ibn Abī al-Iṣbaʿ answered by saying:
«Description in terms of obedience and disobedience is of three kinds. You say: Zayd does not disobey and obeys; its opposite: he does not obey and disobeys; and the intermediate: he does not disobey and does not obey. The first is the highest description, the second the lowest, and the third the middle. The Real, Glorified is He — and He knows best — wished to describe these angels with the highest description. Had He, Mighty and Majestic, confined Himself to His saying "they do not disobey", it would have been possible for it to be continued with your saying "and they do not obey", and that would not fulfil the intended meaning, since what is intended is to describe them with the highest of descriptions. So it was necessary for Him to say "and they do", so that the description is complete. And Allah knows best».
Al-Zamakhsharī raised this difficulty and answered it as follows: «If you ask: are the two clauses not of one meaning? I answer: no; for the meaning of the first is that they accept His commands and hold to them, and do not refuse them or reject them; and the meaning of the second is that they carry out what they are commanded, without being sluggish about it or slack in it. If you ask: Allah has addressed the idolaters who deny the revelation with exactly this, in His saying, the Exalted: "But if you do not, and you never will, then fear the Fire whose fuel is people and stones", and He said: "prepared for the disbelievers", so He made it prepared for the disbelievers; what then is the meaning of His addressing the believers with it? I answer: the grave sinners (al-fussāq), even though their levels are above the levels of the disbelievers, dwell together with the disbelievers in one abode; so it was said to those who believe: protect yourselves, by avoiding grave sin, from dwelling with the disbelievers for whom this described Fire has been prepared. It is also possible that He commands them to guard against apostasy and against regretting having entered Islam». [Translator's note: the source does not mark the end of the quotation; it evidently ends here.]
Ibn al-Munayyir al-Mālikī followed it up in his book al-Intiṣāf, saying: «His first answer is derived from his corrupt principle of believing that grave sinners abide eternally in Hell. Perhaps he raised the question only so as to strain to give an answer to it that would vent what is in himself of this falsehood which he cannot bear to conceal».

dervis-irab:9-12.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَاغْلُظْ عَلَيْهِمْ) be severe with them in speech, and let no leniency or softness take hold of you in dealing with them. In al-Qāmūs: «الغلظة, with the three vowels [on the ghayn], and الغلاظة with kasra, and like ʿinab [i.e. غِلَظ], is the opposite of softness; the verb is like karuma and ḍaraba, so he is غليظ, and غُلاظ like ghurāb; أغلظ له في القول: he was rough with him in speech».

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ جاهِدِ الْكُفَّارَ وَالْمُنافِقِينَ وَاغْلُظْ عَلَيْهِمْ) The i'rab of يا أيها النبي has been given many times. جاهد is an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you"; الكفّار is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and المنافقين is conjoined to الكفّار. اغلظ is an imperative verb conjoined to جاهد, and عليهم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) اغلظ.
(وَمَأْواهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ) The wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); مأواهم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and جهنم the khabar (predicate). بئس is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame, المصير is the fāʿil, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. "it".
(ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا امْرَأَتَ نُوحٍ وَامْرَأَتَ لُوطٍ) A new (mustaʾnaf) statement set out to present a strange case, so that in its light another strange case, resembling it in strangeness, may be understood.
ضرب الله is a verb and its fāʿil; مثلا is a fronted second mafʿūl bihi, and the lām with its genitive is attached to an omitted adjective of مثلا; امرأة نوح is the first mafʿūl bihi, and امرأة لوط is conjoined to امرأة نوح.
(كانَتا تَحْتَ عَبْدَيْنِ مِنْ عِبادِنا صالِحَيْنِ فَخانَتاهُما) The clause is new, set out to explain the striking of the parable. كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the tāʾ is the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine, and the alif is the noun of كان; as for تحت عبدين, the adverb is attached to an omitted khabar of كان; من عبادنا is a naʿt (adjective) of عبدين. فخانتاهما is conjoined; it is a past verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi. The names of the two women and their story will come in the section on benefits.
(فَلَمْ يُغْنِيا عَنْهُما مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً وَقِيلَ ادْخُلَا النَّارَ مَعَ الدَّاخِلِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; لم is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive; يغنيا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the alif is the fāʿil, and عنهما is attached to يغنيا; من الله is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and شيئا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or a mafʿūl bihi. وقيل is conjoined to what precedes; it is a passive past verb, and the clause ادخلا is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); النار is a mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa), and مع الداخلين is an adverb attached to ادخلا. The past verb قيل is imperfect in meaning, i.e. "and it will be said to them".
(وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا امْرَأَتَ فِرْعَوْنَ إِذْ قالَتْ رَبِّ ابْنِ لِي عِنْدَكَ بَيْتاً فِي الْجَنَّةِ) Conjoined to what precedes. إذ is an adverb attached to مثلا; perhaps it is better to say that it is attached to an omitted badal (substitute) from مثلا. The clause قالت is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. ربّ is a one addressed (munādā) in a genitive construct (muḍāf), with the vocative particle omitted; ابن is an imperative verb of supplication, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, and لي is attached to ابن. عندك is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl of the first-person pronoun, or of بيتا, because it precedes it. في الجنة is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) or a badal of His saying عندك, or is attached to ابن.
(وَنَجِّنِي مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ وَعَمَلِهِ وَنَجِّنِي مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ) ونجّني is conjoined to ابن, and من فرعون is attached to نجّني; عمله is conjoined; من القوم is attached to نجّني, and الظالمين is a naʿt of القوم.
(وَمَرْيَمَ ابْنَتَ عِمْرانَ الَّتِي أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَها فَنَفَخْنا فِيهِ مِنْ رُوحِنا) ومريم is conjoined to امرأة فرعون; ابنة is a badal or naʿt of مريم; عمران is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) [Translator's note: the source says «مضاف»], made genitive with fatḥa because it is a diptote, on account of being a proper name and having the added alif and nūn. التي is a naʿt of مريم, and the clause أحصنت فرجها is the ṣila (relative clause) of التي, i.e. she guarded it and protected it from men. فنفخنا is conjoined to أحصنت; فيه is attached to نفخنا; من روحنا is an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl bihi, i.e. "a spirit from Our spirit", من being partitive. The meaning of the blowing has been discussed earlier.
(وَصَدَّقَتْ بِكَلِماتِ رَبِّها وَكُتُبِهِ وَكانَتْ مِنَ الْقانِتِينَ) وصدّقت is conjoined to something omitted and implied, suited to the context, i.e. "so she conceived ʿĪsā and believed". بكلمات is attached to صدّقت, and ربها is muḍāf ilayhi; كتبه is conjoined to كلمات. كانت is a defective past verb whose noun is latent, its implied form being "she", and من القانتين is the khabar. Two views are possible regarding من: first, that it is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya); second, that it is partitive, the masculine being used by way of predominance (taghlīb).

* Rhetoric:
In the striking of the parable there is an allusion (taʿrīḍ) to Ḥafṣa and ʿĀʾisha, mentioned at the beginning of the sūra, and to their lapse in supporting one another against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in what he disliked; and a warning to them in the harshest and severest manner, given that the parable mentions disbelief and the like; and an indication that it is their duty to be, in sincerity and in keeping it secret, like these two believing women, and not to rely on being the wives of the Messenger of Allah, for that merit will not benefit them unless they are sincere. The allusion is to Ḥafṣa because Lūṭ's wife disclosed his secret, just as Ḥafṣa disclosed the Messenger of Allah's secret. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «In the two parables there is a lesson for the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, since their reproach came earlier; but this is far-fetched, because the text being about the disbelievers makes this unlikely».

* Benefits:
The commentators mentioned that Nūḥ's wife used to tell his people that he was mad, and her name was Wāhila, with the hāʾ before the lām, and it has been said the reverse; and that Lūṭ's wife used to guide his people to his guests when they lodged with him, by night by lighting a fire and by day by making smoke, and her name was Wāʿila, with the ʿayn before the lām, and it has been said the reverse. As for Pharaoh's wife, her name was Āsiya bint Muzāḥim, and she had true insight regarding Yūsuf [Translator's note: so in the source; the story — "a comfort of the eye for me and for you" (al-Qaṣaṣ 28:9) — concerns Mūsā, not Yūsuf] when she said: "a comfort of the eye for me and for you". Among her merits is that she chose being killed over kingship, and the torment of this world over the luxury in which she used to live.
Moreover, there is consensus that the wife of a prophet never committed fornication. It has been said that their betrayal was hypocrisy, and it has been said that they betrayed them by tale-bearing.

farraa:1-2.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَآ أَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ لَكَ﴾.
It came down concerning Māriya the Copt. The Prophet ﷺ used to assign a day to each of his wives. When it was ʿĀʾisha's day, Ḥafṣa bint ʿUmar visited her, so her [Ḥafṣa's] house was empty, and the Prophet ﷺ sent for Māriya the Copt, and she was with the Prophet ﷺ in Ḥafṣa's dwelling. Ḥafṣa came to her dwelling and found the curtain let down. The Prophet ﷺ came out and said: Will you keep this secret for me? She said: Yes. He said: Then she is forbidden to me — meaning Māriya — and I tell you that your father and Abū Bakr will rule after me. Ḥafṣa told ʿĀʾisha the news, and revelation came down to the Prophet ﷺ about it. He called Ḥafṣa and said: What made you do what you did? She said to him: And who told you that I said that to ʿĀʾisha? He said: "The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me". Then he divorced Ḥafṣa with one divorce and kept away from his wives for twenty-nine days. And there came down to him: ﴿لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَآ أَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ لَكَ﴾, regarding intimacy with Māriya. Then He said: ﴿قَدْ فَرَضَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ تَحِلَّةَ أَيْمَانِكُمْ﴾, meaning: the expiation of your oaths. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ freed a slave and returned to Māriya.
[Al-Farrāʾ] said: Ḥibbān told me this interpretation from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās. Then He said: "عرف بعضه" — He is saying: he made Ḥafṣa aware of part of what was said and left part. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read "عَرَف", light.
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl al-Marwazī told me, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī: "عَرَف", light.
Al-Farrāʾ told us: and a shaykh of Banū Asad — meaning al-Kisāʾī — told me, from Nuʿaym, from Abū ʿAmr, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: when a man recited to him "عَرَّف بعضه" with doubling, he would pelt him with pebbles. It is as if those who say عَرَف, light, mean: he was angered by it and requited it, as you say to a man who wrongs you: By Allah, I will surely "know" that against you (i.e. repay you for it). And by my life, he did requite Ḥafṣa by divorcing her; and this is a good interpretation. [And it is reported of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī that he read عَرَف light, like Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.]

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلاً لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾.
This is a parable by which ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa are meant; He struck the parable for them both, saying: The faith of their husbands did not benefit the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot, and their hypocrisy did not harm their husbands; likewise the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ would not benefit you two if you did not believe, and your sins would not harm him. Then He said: ﴿وضَرَبَ اللهُ مَثَلاً لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا امْرَأَتَ فِرْعَوْن﴾, so He commanded them both to be like Āsiya and like Mary daughter of ʿImrān, who guarded her chastity (farj). Al-farj here is the neck-opening of her shift; it is mentioned that Jibrīl ﷺ blew into the opening of her garment. Every opening in a shift, whether a tear or otherwise, can be called farj. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَالَهَا مِنْ فُرُوجٍ﴾, meaning the sky has no cracks or rifts.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿إِن تَتُوبَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ﴾.
He means ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa. That is because ʿĀʾisha said: O Messenger of Allah, as for the day of the others, you complete it, but on my day you do what you did? So there came down: "If you two repent to Allah" from your collaborating against the Prophet ﷺ ﴿فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا﴾: they have deviated and inclined. ﴿وَإِن تَظَاهَرَا عَلَيْهِ﴾: [if] you collaborate against him. ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it light, and the people of the Hijaz read it: "تظَّاهرا" with doubling. ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ مَوْلاَهُ﴾: his protector against you both, ﴿وَجِبْرِيلُ وَصَالِحُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: such as Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, in whom there is no hypocrisy. Then He said: ﴿وَالْمَلاَئِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ﴾: after those, He means helpers, and He did not say ظهراء. If someone said that ظهير belongs to Jibrīl, the righteous believers and the angels [together], it would be correct; but it is good to make ظهير belong to the angels specifically, because of His saying (والملائكة) — after the help of these — [are] ظهير.
As for His saying: ﴿وَصَالِحُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, it is singular in the sense of a plural, as you say: لا يأتينى إلا سائس الحرب (none shall come to me except the manager of war): whoever is capable of managing war has been told to come, whether one or more. Similar to it: ﴿وَالسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهُمَا﴾: this is general [201/b], not one or two. Likewise His saying: ﴿والَّلذانِ يأْتِيَانِهَا مِنكُمْ فَآذُوهما﴾, and likewise: ﴿إنّ الإِنْسَانَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ﴾ and ﴿إِنَّ الإِنْسَانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعاً﴾ — in much of the Qur'an the singular conveys the meaning of the plural.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read: "أنْ يُبْدلَهُ", light, and the people of the Hijaz read: "أن يبَدِّله" [with doubling]; and both are correct: أبدلت and بدّلت.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿سَائِحَاتٍ﴾.
They are women who fast. He said: We think that the one who fasts is called سائح (wanderer) only because the wanderer has no provisions with him and eats only where he finds [food], so it is as if it were taken from that. And Allah knows best.
The Arabs say of a horse when it stands without fodder: صائم (fasting). That is because it has two meals, a meal in the morning and a meal in the evening, so it is likened to the predawn meal of a human being and his breaking of the fast.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿قُوۤاْ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ﴾.
Teach your families that by which they ward off sins; teach them that.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying: ﴿تَوْبَةً نَّصُوحاً﴾.
The people of Medina and al-Aʿmash read it with fatḥa on the nūn, and it is reported of ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan [that they read] "نُصُوحاً" with ḍamma on the nūn. It is as if those who say "نُصوحاً" intend the maṣdar (verbal noun), like قُعودا, while those who say "نَصوحا" make it a description of the repentance. Its meaning is: when he repents of that sin, he resolves in himself never to return to it.
His saying: ﴿يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا﴾.
Not everyone who enters Paradise says this; only the lowest of them in rank says it. That is because the foremost, as has been mentioned, pass over the Bridge (al-ṣirāṭ) like lightning, some like the wind, some like a swift horse, and some crawling and creeping. It is these who say: ﴿رَبَّنَا أتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا﴾ so that we may be saved.
If a reader read "ويدخلْكم" in the jussive, it would be a valid way, because the answer [is] to عسى: the فاء is implied in [the answer to] عسى, and "entering" is intended as conjoined to the place of the فاء. But no one read it so. Similar to it: ﴿فَأَصَّدَقَ وأكُنْ مِنَ الصَّالِحِين﴾.
Similar is the poet's saying:
فأبلونى بليتكُم لعلى * أصالحكم، واستدرجْ نَويَّا
(So grant me your favour, perhaps I may make peace with you, and draw my distant company [back] step by step.)
He put it in the jussive because he intended joining it back to لعلّى.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The clause «تحرم», the answer to the vocative, is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun «لِمَ» are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تحرم»; the clause «تبتغي» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تحرم»; the clause «والله غفور» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «قد فرض» is resumptive; the clause «والله مولاكم» is resumptive; the clause «وهو العليم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «والله مولاكم». «تَحِلَّة» is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «حلَّل», originally تَحْلِلَة, and it is accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The wāw is resumptive; «إذ» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the implied verb «اذكر» (remember); the clause «فلما نبأت به» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «أَسرَّ»; the clause «عرّف» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the clause «فلما نبأها» is conjoined to the clause «نبأت به»; the clause «أنبأك» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «مَنْ»; the clause «قال» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «هو» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl). His words «وجبريل»: a mubtadaʾ (subject), what follows it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it, and «ظهير» is the khabar (predicate) of them all; «ظهير» is singular because it is on the pattern faʿīl; and «جبريل» is mentioned in the helping twice: once by being named explicitly, and once by being included in the generality of the angels.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «عسى» is incomplete (nāqiṣa), and the maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يبدله» is the khabar (predicate) of «عسى»; the clause «إن طلقكن» is parenthetical, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, what precedes indicating it; «أزواجا» is a second object; «خيرا» and what follows it are naʿts (adjectives); the preposition phrase «منكنَّ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خيرا».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: His words «قوا»: an imperative from الوقاية (protection), its pattern being عُوا; the fāʾ [of the root] was omitted because in the imperfect it occurs between a yāʾ and a kasra, and the imperative is modelled on it; the clause «وقودها الناس» is a naʿt (adjective) of «نارا», and the clause «عليها ملائكة» is a second naʿt; the clause «لا يَعْصُون» is a naʿt of «ملائكة»; «ما» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ما أمرهم» is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from the Divine Name, i.e.: they do not disobey Allah's command.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «إنما تجزون» is resumptive; «ما» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: «نصوحا» is an attribute of «توبة» by way of intensification, on the basis that it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) itself; the clause «عسى ربكم» is resumptive, and the maṣdar «أن يكفِّر» is the khabar (predicate) of «عسى»; the adverb «يوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يدخلكم»; the clause «نورهم يسعى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «النبي والذين آمنوا معه»; the clause «يقولون» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «أيديهم»; the clause «إنك على كل شيء قدير» is resumptive within the scope of the answer to the vocative.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause «ومأواهم جهنم» is resumptive, and the clause «وبئس المصير» is resumptive; the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e.: Jahannam.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: «امرأة» is a badal (substitute) from «مثلا»; the preposition phrase «للذين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «مثلا»; the clause «كانتا» is an explanation of «المثل»; the preposition phrase «من عبادنا» is attached to a naʿt of «عبدين»; the two preposition phrases «عنهما من الله» are attached to the verb «يغنيا»; «شيئا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause «وقيل» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يغنيا».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «امرأة» is a badal (substitute) from «مثلا»; «إذ» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ضرب»; the adverb «عندك» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «بيتا»; the preposition phrase «في الجنة» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «بيتا».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: His words «مريم»: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «امرأة»; «ابنت» is a badal (substitute); «التي» is a naʿt (adjective) of «مريم».

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He, تبتغي: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the latent pronoun in تحرم.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying تَحِلَّة: accusative by فرض. Its pattern is تَفْعِلة, and its origin is تَحْلِلة; then the vowel of the first lām was transferred onto the حاء and [the lām] was assimilated into the second.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying نبأت بِهِ: the object is omitted, its implied form being "she informed her companion of it" (نبأت به صاحبتها), meaning ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa, may Allah be pleased with them both; Ḥafṣa was the one who told ʿĀʾisha the secret. Likewise the object is also omitted from His saying, Exalted is He, عرف بعضه, in the reading of whoever doubles the رآء, i.e. "he made her acquainted with part of it", i.e. part of what she had disclosed to her companion, "and turned away from part", out of generosity on his part ﷺ, so he did not make her acquainted with it. As for whoever reads the رآء without doubling [عَرَف], it is in the sense of "he requited part of it and did not requite part", out of kindness on his part ﷺ. It is not good for its meaning to be that he did not know part of it, because Allah has told us that He made His Prophet aware of it; so it is not possible that He made him aware of what she disclosed and he knew part of what He made him aware of and not another part, or knew part and was ignorant of part.
His saying فإن الله هُوَ مَوْلَاهُ: هو is a separating pronoun (fāṣila), and مولاه is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ. It is also possible that هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and مولاه the khabar, the clause being the khabar of إنّ; on this view you pause on مولاه and do not go beyond it.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t:
His saying قُلُوبكُمَا: القلب was put in the plural, although they are two, only because anything of which there is only one in a person, when its like is joined to it, is [expressed as] a plural. It is also said: because the dual is a plural, since it is the joining of one thing to another.
His saying وَجِبْرِيل: a mubtadaʾ (subject), what follows it is conjoined to it, and ظهير is the khabar (predicate). It is also possible that وجبريل is conjoined to مولاه, المولى meaning the protecting friend (الولي); on this view you pause on جبريل, and وصالح المؤمنين is a mubtadaʾ, والملائكة is conjoined, and ظهير is the khabar. It is also possible that وصالح المؤمنين is conjoined to جبريل, and جبريل conjoined to مولاه, المولى meaning the protecting friend, because the angels and the believers are the protecting friends of the prophets and their helpers; on this view you pause on المؤمنين, and His saying والملائكة is a mubtadaʾ and ظهير its khabar. However, what is customary among the readers is to pause on مولاه, and جبريل is a mubtadaʾ with which one begins.

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying أَن يُبدلهُ: أن is in the position of the accusative, the khabar (predicate) of عسى; like it is أن يكفر.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying قوا أَنفسكُم: قوا is a verb whose first and third radicals are both weak. The first radical (fāʾ) is omitted because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra in your saying يقي, according to the doctrine of the Basrans. The Kufans said it was only omitted to distinguish between the transitive and the intransitive verb: so it was omitted in يعد and يقي because they are transitive, and kept in يوجل because it is intransitive. But it follows for them that they should not omit it in يرم and يثق, because they are intransitive, while omission is necessary in both. The third radical (lām) is omitted because it is quiescent and the wāw after it is quiescent. The nūn is omitted because of indeclinability (bināʾ) according to the Basrans, and because of the jussive according to the Kufans. Its origin is أوقيوا; the wāw was omitted for the reason we mentioned, so the connective alif was dispensed with; then the vowel of the yāʾ was transferred onto the قاف, and [the yāʾ] was omitted because it was quiescent and the wāw after it was quiescent, so it became قوا. It is also said, rather, that the ḍamma was removed from the yāʾ for lightness, and [the yāʾ] was omitted because it was quiescent and the wāw after it was quiescent, and the قاف was given a ḍamma for the sake of the wāw, so that it would not change into a yāʾ and the meaning be altered. Parallels to this have preceded.
His saying وَمَرْيَم ابنت عمرَان: مريم is accusative by conjunction with مثلا, and ابنة is a naʿt (adjective) of it or a badal (substitute). مريم is a diptote because of femininity and definiteness. It is said that it is a foreign (non-Arabic) noun, and it is also said that it is Arabic.

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying ضرب الله مثلا للَّذين كفرُوا امْرَأَة نوح وَامْرَأَة لوط: [مثلا and امرأة نوح are] the two objects of ضرب. It is also said that امرأة نوح is a badal (substitute) of مثل, on the assumption of "the likeness of the wife of Noah" (مثل امرأة نوح); then the second مثل was omitted because the first indicates it.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿يا أيها النبي﴾: «يا» is a vocative particle; «أي» is the one addressed (munādā), a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma in the position of an accusative (manṣūb); «ها» is for drawing attention; and «النبي» is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾.
﴿لم تحرم ما أحل الله لك تبتغي مرضات أزواجك﴾: the lām is a preposition, and «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تحرم». «ما» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause ﴿أحل الله﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. «لك» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أحل﴾; the clause «تبتغي» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تحرم»; and «مرضاة أزواجك» is a mafʿūl bihi.
﴿والله غفور رحيم﴾: «الله» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «غفور» is a khabar (predicate), and «رحيم» is a second khabar.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿قد فرض الله لكم تحلة أيمانكم﴾: «قد» is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); «فرض الله» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «فرض»; «تحلة» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «أيمانكم» is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿والله مولاكم وهو العليم الحكيم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «الله» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «مولاكم» is the khabar (predicate); «هو» is a mubtadaʾ, «العليم» is a first khabar, and «الحكيم» is a second khabar.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وإذ أسر النبي إلى بعض أزواجه حديثا﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being «اذكر» (remember); the clause ﴿أسر النبي﴾ is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) as a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and «حديثًا» is a mafʿūl bihi.
﴿فلما نبأت به وأظهره الله عليه عرف بعضه وأعرض عن بعض﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «لما» is an adverb in the sense of «حين» (when), or a linking [particle] containing the meaning of condition; the clause «نبأت» is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. «نبأت» in the verse is transitive to two [objects], the first of which is omitted, and the second is made genitive by the bāʾ, i.e. «نبأت به غيرها» (she informed another woman of it). «وأظهره»: the wāw is a conjunction, «أظهره» is a verb and its object, and «الله» is the fāʿil (agent); «عليه» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أظهره﴾. The clause «عرف» has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; «بعضه» is a mafʿūl bihi; «أعرض» is conjoined to «عرف»; «عن بعض» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أعرض﴾; and the second object of «عرف» is omitted, i.e. «عرفها بعض ما فعلت» (he made her know part of what she had done).
﴿فلما نبأها به قالت من أنبأك هذا قال نبأني العليم الخبير﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «لما» is a temporal adverb (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya), or a linking [particle] containing the meaning of condition in any case; «نبأها» is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; the clause «قالت» has no grammatical position; «من» is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «أنبأك» is the khabar (predicate), the kāf being the first object and «هذا» the second object; «قال» is a past verb; the clause «نبأني العليم الخبير» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying); «العليم» is the fāʿil of «نبأني», and «الخبير» is an adjective (ṣifa).

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿إن تتوبا إلى الله فقد صغت قلوبكما﴾: «إن» is conditional; «تتوبا» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its being jussive (majzūm) being the dropping of the nūn; the alif is the fāʿil (agent); «إلى الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تتوبا﴾; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being: «يتب عليكما» (He will turn to you in forgiveness). The fāʾ is causal (taʿlīliyya); «قد» is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); «صغت», i.e. inclined, is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on a fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the tāʾ is the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine; and «قلوبكما» is the fāʿil of «صغت».
﴿وإن تظاهرا عليه فإن الله هو مولاه وجبريل وصالح المؤمنين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «إن» is conditional; «تظاهرا» is the protasis, the sign of its being jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the alif is the fāʿil; «عليه» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تظاهرا﴾; the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being: «يجد ناصرًا» (he will find a helper). The fāʾ is causal; «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); the Name of Majesty is its noun; «هو» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); and «مولاه» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن». «جبريل» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «صالح المؤمنين» is conjoined to «جبريل». It has also been said: «جبريل» and «صالح المؤمنين» are both conjoined to the position of «إن» and its noun, so that the khabar of them all is «مولاه»; on the view that it is a mubtadaʾ, the khabar is His saying: «ظهير».
﴿والملائكة بعد ذلك ظهير﴾: «الملائكة» is conjoined to what precedes; or: a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «ظهير».

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿عسى ربه إن طلقكن أن يبدله أزواجا خيرا منكن﴾: «عسى» is a past verb, one of the verbs of hope (afʿāl al-rajāʾ), and «ربه» is its noun; «إن» is conditional; «طلقكن» is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); «أن» is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; «يبدله» is an imperfect verb made accusative (manṣūb) by «أن», and «أن» together with what falls within its scope is the khabar (predicate) of «عسى»; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. «فعسى» (then it may be). «أزواجًا» is the second mafʿūl bihi, «خيرًا» is an adjective (ṣifa), and «منكن» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خيرًا﴾.
﴿مسلمات مؤمنات قانتات تائبات عابدات سائحات ثيبات وأبكارا﴾: «مسلمات» is a second naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أزواجًا﴾, or a ḥāl (circumstantial), or accusative by way of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ); and what follows it are multiple adjectives.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position. «يا» is a vocative particle; «أي» is the one addressed (munādā), a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma in the position of an accusative (manṣūb); «ها» is for drawing attention; «الذين» is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾; «آمنوا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم نارًا وقودها الناس والحجارة﴾: «قوا» is an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; «أنفسكم» is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «أهليكم» is conjoined to «أنفسكم», the sign of its being accusative being the yāʾ, because it is attached (mulḥaq) to the sound masculine plural; «نارًا» is the second mafʿūl bihi; «وقودها» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «الناس» the khabar (predicate), or the reverse; «الحجارة» is conjoined to «النار» «[Translator's note: so in the source; it is conjoined to «الناس».]»; and the clause «وقودها الناس» is an adjective of ﴿نارًا﴾.
﴿عليها ملائكة غلاظ شداد لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم ويفعلون ما يؤمرون﴾: the clause is a second adjective of ﴿نارًا﴾. «عليها» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar; «ملائكة» is a postponed mubtadaʾ; «غلاظ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «ملائكة», and «شداد» is a second naʿt. «لا» is negating; «يعصون الله» is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya); «أمرهم» is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar formed from ﴿ما﴾ with what it governs is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from ﴿الله﴾, in the accusative, or it is accusative by removal of the preposition. The clause ﴿أمرهم﴾ is the ṣila of the particle-relative ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position. «ويفعلون»: the wāw is a conjunction, and «يفعلون» is an imperfect verb in the nominative and its fāʿil; ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi; the clause «يؤمرون» is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; and the referring pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. «به».

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين كفروا﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position. «يا» is a vocative particle; «أي» is the one addressed (munādā), a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma in the position of an accusative (manṣūb); «ها» is for drawing attention; «الذين» is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾; «كفروا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿لا تعتذروا اليوم إنما تجزون ما كنتم تعملون﴾: «لا» is prohibitive; «تعتذروا» is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive «لا»; «اليوم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تعتذروا﴾; and the clause is the object of an omitted saying, i.e. that is said to them upon entering the Fire. «إنما» is [«إنّ»] restrained [from governing] by the restraining [«ما»] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); «تجزون» is an imperfect verb built for the one whose agent is not named (passive), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); «ما» is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause «كنتم» is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; and the clause «تعملون» is the khabar (predicate) of «كنتم».

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
