﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا﴾: «يا» is a vocative particle; «أي» is the one addressed (munādā), a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma in the position of an accusative (manṣūb); «ها» is for drawing attention; «الذين» is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾; «آمنوا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿توبوا إلى الله توبة نصوحا﴾: «توبوا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; «إلى الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿توبوا﴾; «توبة» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and «نصوحًا» is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿توبة﴾.
﴿عسى ربكم أن يكفر عنكم سيئاتكم﴾: «عسى» is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb, one of the verbs of hope (afʿāl al-rajāʾ), and «ربكم» is its noun; «أن» together with what falls within its scope is in the place of an accusative as the khabar (predicate) of «عسى»; «عنكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يكفر﴾; and «سيئاتكم» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ويدخلكم جنات تجري من تحتها الأنهار﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «يدخلكم» is conjoined to «يكفر», and the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi; «جنات» is a second mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause «تجري» is a naʿt of ﴿جنات﴾; «من تحتها» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تجري﴾; and «الأنهار» is the fāʿil of «تجري».
﴿يوم لا يخزي الله النبي﴾: ﴿يوم﴾ is an adverb attached to ﴿يدخلكم﴾; ﴿لا﴾ is negating; ﴿يخزي الله﴾ is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause ﴿لا يخزي﴾ is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the annexation of the adverb to it; and ﴿النبي﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi.
﴿والذين آمنوا معه نورهم يسعى بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «الذين» is a relative noun in the position of an accusative, conjoined to «النبي»; «نورهم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «يسعى» is the khabar; the clause ﴿نورهم يسعى﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿النبي والذين آمنوا معه﴾. Or the wāw is resumptive, the clause after it being resumptive with no grammatical position, «الذين» being a mubtadaʾ, and the clause ﴿نورهم يسعى﴾ its khabar. ﴿بين﴾ is an adverb attached to ﴿يسعى﴾, and «أيديهم» is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «بأيمانهم» is conjoined to the adverb, attached to what it is attached to.
﴿يقولون ربنا أتمم لنا نورنا﴾: the clause is circumstantial, in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl from ﴿النبي والذين آمنوا معه﴾. «ربنا» is the one addressed, a muḍāf; «أتمم» is a verb of supplication, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being «أنت» (You); ﴿لنا﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «أتمم»; «نورنا» is the object of «أتمم»; and the clause ﴿ربنا أتمم لنا نورنا﴾ is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying).
﴿واغفر لنا﴾: «اغفر» is a verb of supplication, indeclinable on sukūn, and the fāʿil is «أنت»; «لنا» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿اغفر﴾; and the clause ﴿اغفر لنا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿أتمم لنا﴾ within the scope of the saying.
﴿إنك على كل شيء قدير﴾: ﴿إنك﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) and the kāf is its noun; ﴿على كل﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿قدير﴾; ﴿شيء﴾ is a muḍāf ilayhi; and ﴿قدير﴾ is the khabar of «إن», in the nominative (marfūʿ).

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿يا أيها النبي﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position. «يا» is a vocative particle; «أي» is the one addressed (munādā), a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma in the position of an accusative (manṣūb); «ها» is for drawing attention; and «النبي» is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾.
﴿جاهد الكفار والمنافقين واغلظ عليهم﴾: «جاهد» is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir), its implied form being «أنت» (you); «الكفار» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «المنافقين» is conjoined to «الكفار»; «اغلظ» is an imperative verb conjoined to «جاهد»; and «عليهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اغلظ﴾.
﴿ومأواهم جهنم وبئس المصير﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); «مأواهم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «جهنم» is the khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿ومأواهم جهنم﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position. «بئس» is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; «المصير» is the fāʿil; and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e.: «هي» (it).

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿ضرب الله مثلا للذين كفروا امرأة نوح وامرأة لوط﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position. «ضرب الله» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «مثلًا» is a fronted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the lām and what it puts in the genitive are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿مثلًا﴾; «امرأة نوح» is the first mafʿūl bihi; and «امرأة لوط» is conjoined to «امرأة نوح».
﴿كانتا تحت عبدين من عبادنا صالحين فخانتاهما﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. «كان» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the tāʾ is the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine; the alif is the noun of «كان»; «تحت عبدين»: the adverb is attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of «كان»; «من عبادنا» is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عبدين﴾; «فخانتاهما» is conjoined, and it is a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi.
﴿فلم يغنيا عنهما من الله شيئا وقيل ادخلا النار مع الداخلين﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «لم» is a particle of negation, of conversion [to the past] and of the jussive; «يغنيا» is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by «لم», the sign of its being jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the alif is the fāʿil; «عنهما» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يغنيا﴾; «من الله»: «من» is a preposition and the Name of Majesty is a genitive noun, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿يغنيا﴾; «شيئًا» stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), or it is a mafʿūl bihi. «قيل» is conjoined to what precedes, and it is a past verb built for the one whose agent is not named (passive); the clause «ادخلا» is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying); «النار» is a mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); and «مع الداخلين» is an adverb attached to ﴿ادخلا﴾.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿وضرب الله مثلا للذين آمنوا امرأت فرعون﴾: «ضرب الله» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «مثلًا» is a fronted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the lām and what it puts in the genitive are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿مثلا﴾; and «امرأة فرعون» is the first mafʿūl bihi.
﴿إذ قالت رب ابن لي عندك بيتا في الجنة﴾: ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb attached to ﴿ضرب﴾, even though the striking [of the parable] appears later, or attached to «المثَل» (the parable); the clause ﴿قالت﴾ is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) as a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «رب» is the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, from which the vocative particle has been omitted; «ابنِ» is a verb of supplication, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter; «لي» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ابنِ﴾; «عندك» is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the first-person pronoun, or from ﴿بيتًا﴾ because it precedes it; and «في الجنة» is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) or a badal (substitute) for His saying «عندك», or [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to «ابنِ».
﴿ونجني من فرعون وعمله ونجني من القوم الظالمين﴾: «نجني» is conjoined to «ابنِ»; «من فرعون» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نجني﴾; «عمله» is conjoined; «من القوم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نجني﴾; and «الظالمين» is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿القوم﴾.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿ومريم ابنت عمران التي أحصنت فرجها﴾: «مريم» is conjoined to «امرأة فرعون»; «ابنة» is a badal (substitute) of, or a naʿt (adjective) of, ﴿مريم﴾; «عمران» is a muḍāf «[Translator's note: so in the source; «عمران» is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).]» and is made genitive by the fatḥa, because it is a diptote on account of being a proper name and having the added alif and nūn; ﴿التي﴾ is a relative noun in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as a naʿt of ﴿مريم﴾; and the clause ﴿أحصنت فرجها﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿التي﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿فنفخنا فيه من روحنا﴾: «فنفخنا» is conjoined to «أحصنت»; «فيه» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نفخنا﴾; «من روحنا» is an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. «روحًا من روحنا» (a spirit of Our spirit); and «من» is partitive (tabʿīḍ).
﴿وصدقت بكلمات ربها وكتبه﴾: «صدقت» is conjoined to an omitted [verb], implied in a way suited to the context, i.e. «حملت بعيسى وصدقت» (she conceived ʿĪsā and believed); «بكلمات» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿صدقت﴾; «ربها» is a muḍāf ilayhi; and «كتبه» is conjoined to «كلمات».
﴿وكانت من القانتين﴾: «كانت» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun being latent (mustatir), its implied form being «هي» (she); «من القانتين» is the khabar (predicate); and «من» is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya); or: for partition, the masculine being used by way of predominance (taghlīb).

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ ما أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكَ: this is «ما», to which the lām was prefixed, and the alif was dropped to distinguish between the interrogative and the declarative, and because it has become joined to the lām. Pausing on it outside the Qur'an: "limah", the hāʾ being brought to make the vowel clear; in the Qur'an one does not pause on it. They disagreed about what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made unlawful. Mālik ibn Anas reported from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made the mother of Ibrāhīm unlawful [to himself] and said: "By Allah, I will not touch you." Abū Jaʿfar said: on this view, the expiation was only for the oath, not for his saying "you are unlawful to me". Masrūq and al-Shaʿbī said likewise. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: whoever says of something lawful "it is unlawful to me" owes the expiation of an oath. Qatāda said likewise. Masrūq said: if he says to his wife "you are unlawful to me", he owes nothing, neither expiation nor divorce, because he is lying in this. It has been said: he owes the expiation of an oath, and the holder of this view interpreted the verse [accordingly]. And it has been said:
she is divorced three times if the marriage has been consummated, and once if it has not. It has been said: it is one irrevocable divorce; and it has been said: one revocable divorce. It is reported from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, concerning this verse, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had only made honey unlawful to himself. Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind reported from al-Shaʿbī, from Masrūq, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made [something] unlawful and took an oath of abstention (ālā), and he was reproached concerning the prohibition and given expiation (ʿātaba) [Translator's note: so in the text, «وعاتب في الإيلاء»; the expected wording is «وكفّر في الإيلاء» "and made expiation for the oath of abstention"] concerning the oath of abstention. Abū Jaʿfar said: it is not known in any dialect that one who makes the lawful unlawful is called "one who swears an oath" (ḥālif). تَبْتَغِي is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). مَرْضاتَ أَزْواجِكَ: this is the tāʾ of the feminine; if it were the tāʾ of the plural, it would take kasra [in the accusative]. وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ: that is, to His creatures, and He has forgiven you. رَحِيمٌ: He does not punish whoever repents.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: قَدْ فَرَضَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ تَحِلَّةَ أَيْمانِكُمْ: that is, He has made it clear. وَاللَّهُ مَوْلاكُمْ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); that is, He takes charge of you with His help. وَهُوَ الْعَلِيمُ: of the interests of His servants. الْحَكِيمُ: in His management.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَتْ بِهِ: the object is omitted, i.e. she informed her companion of it; and they were ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa — there is no disagreement about that. They disagreed about what he confided to her. It has been said: it is what he told her about his drinking honey at the home of one of his wives. It has been said: it is what took place between him and the mother of Ibrāhīm. And it has been said: it is his informing her that Abū Bakr would be the caliph after him; we have mentioned this with its chain of transmission. فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَتْ بِهِ وَأَظْهَرَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ وَأَعْرَضَ عَنْ بَعْضٍ: here too the object is omitted: he made known to her part of it, saying: "I have learned such-and-such through revelation". وَأَعْرَضَ عَنْ بَعْضٍ: he did not mention it, out of graciousness and modesty. Al-Kisāʾī's reading is "ʿarafa baʿḍahu" [with the rāʾ unstressed] [Translator's note: the vowelled text does not show the variant], and Abū ʿUbayd rejected it in harsh terms, saying: if it were so, it would be "he knew part of it and disowned part". Abū Jaʿfar said:
this rejection is not binding; the reading is well known from a group, among them Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, and we have explained its soundness. فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَها بِهِ قالَتْ مَنْ أَنْبَأَكَ هذا: "nabbaʾa" and "anbaʾa" have one meaning, so it brought both forms together, and after it قالَ نَبَّأَنِيَ الْعَلِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ.
[Sūrat al-Taḥrīm (66): Verse 3]
وَإِذْ أَسَرَّ النَّبِيُّ إِلى بَعْضِ أَزْواجِهِ حَدِيثاً فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَتْ بِهِ وَأَظْهَرَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ وَأَعْرَضَ عَنْ بَعْضٍ فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَها بِهِ قالَتْ مَنْ أَنْبَأَكَ هذا قالَ نَبَّأَنِيَ الْعَلِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ (3)
إِنْ تَتُوبا إِلَى اللَّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُما: that is, they inclined towards liking what the Prophet ﷺ disliked, namely his making unlawful what was lawful for him. وَإِنْ تَظاهَرا عَلَيْهِ: the origin is "tataẓāharā"; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ẓāʾ. The Kufans read "taẓāharā" ] with the tāʾ dropped. فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ مَوْلاهُ: that is, his protector with help. وَجِبْرِيلُ وَصالِحُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: they disagreed about "ṣāliḥ al-muʾminīn" (the righteous of the believers). Among the soundest things said about it is that it refers to every righteous one of the believers, and no single person is specified by it except by authoritative instruction (tawqīf). It is reported that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, is meant by it; he was the one who entered into this affair and spoke about it, and the Qur'an was revealed with some of what he said in this affair. It has been said: it is Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both; and it has been said: it is ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him. We have mentioned that with its chain of transmission. The position of al-Farrāʾ is the view we began with: a singular that indicates a plurality. Likewise وَالْمَلائِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ: "ẓahīr" conveys the plural. We have mentioned other things about it besides this.
[Translator's note: "tataẓāharā" above should read "tataẓāharā" (تتظاهرا).]

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: إِنْ [Translator's note: so in the text; the word meant is «أن» (an)] is in the position of the accusative by "ʿasā", and the condition is parenthetical. The reading of the Kufans is "an yubdilahu azwājan khayran minkunna" [with the lighter form of the verb]. It has been said [concerning] "khayran minkunna": that if they had persisted in what they were doing until they drove him to divorce them, He would have given him in exchange [wives] better than them. مُسْلِماتٍ مُؤْمِناتٍ قانِتاتٍ تائِباتٍ عابِداتٍ سائِحاتٍ ثَيِّباتٍ: all of it is a naʿt (adjective) of "azwāj". The singular is "zawj", and an anomalous dialect form is "zawja". وَأَبْكاراً: conjoined, also included in the naʿt.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ ناراً: the verb from this is "waqā yaqī" according to all the grammarians, and the origin according to them is "waqā yawqī". Then they disagreed about the reason for dropping the wāw. The Basrans said: the wāw was dropped because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra while being quiescent; it was not dropped in "yawjalu", because after it there is a fatḥa, and the fatḥa is not found heavy. The Kufans said: the wāw was dropped for the transitive verb and kept in the intransitive to make a distinction; so they said in the transitive "waʿada yaʿidu" and in the intransitive "wajila yawjalu". They countered the Basrans with the Arabs' saying "wasiʿa yasaʿu", where the wāw was dropped though followed by a fatḥa, and likewise "walagha yalaghu". The argument for the Basrans is that the origin is "wasiʿa yawsiʿu"; the wāw was dropped for the reason given above, and the sīn was given fatḥa because the word contains one of the guttural letters. The Kufans said: the wāw was dropped because it is a transitive verb. The Basrans replied to them with the Arabs' saying "warima yarimu": this is intransitive and the wāw has been dropped from it; and likewise "yathiqu". So their claim that it is dropped only from the transitive is broken. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a clear rebuttal. If «قوا» had come in its original form, it would be "īqiyū" (ايقيوا). أَنْفُسَكُمْ: accusative by "qū", just as one says "akrim nafsaka" (honour yourself), and one may not say "akrimka". As for the statement of Sībawayh: [it is not said] because they made do without it by saying "akrim nafsaka". Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: this was not permitted because a thing cannot be agent and object at the same time. As for the Kufans, they were inconsistent in this: at times they say it is not permissible, as the Basrans say, and at times they report from the Arabs that it is permitted; they reported "ʿadimtunī" (I lost myself), whereas the Basrans permit none of this. وَأَهْلِيكُمْ is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to "anfusakum".
Among the questions of al-Farrāʾ concerning «وأهليكم»: why is it made quiescent while in the accusative position? The answer is that the yāʾ is the sign of the accusative, as in your saying "raʾaytu al-Zaydīna", and the nūn was dropped because of the construct (iḍāfa). Al-Farrāʾ reported that some of the Arabs say "ahla" for the feminine. «نارا»: a second object. وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of "the Fire". وَالْحِجارَةُ: conjoined to "al-nās". عَلَيْها مَلائِكَةٌ غِلاظٌ شِدادٌ: that is, harsh towards the disobedient and severe with them; and it has been said: «شداد» means strong. لا يَعْصُونَ اللَّهَ ما أَمَرَهُمْ: two objects, with the preposition omitted, i.e. "in what He commands them". وَيَفْعَلُونَ ما يُؤْمَرُونَ: the pronoun referring back to "mā" is omitted; if you take it as maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), you need no returning pronoun.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لا تَعْتَذِرُوا الْيَوْمَ: the nūn was dropped for the jussive by the prohibition. إِنَّما تُجْزَوْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ: «إنما» carries the meaning of affirmation and establishing.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: تَوْبَةً: a maṣdar (verbal noun). نَصُوحاً: its naʿt (adjective), i.e. in which you are sincere to yourselves. عَسى رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ يُكَفِّرَ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئاتِكُمْ وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ: al-Farrāʾ permitted "wa-yudkhilkum" in the jussive, conjoined to the position, because "ʿasā" is in the position of the jussive in meaning, since it is the answer to the command; he took it as meaning "fa-ʿasā", and conjoined «ويدخلكم» to the position of the fāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a severe distortion (taʿassuf). يَوْمَ لا يُخْزِي اللَّهُ النَّبِيَّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ: «الذين» is in the position of the accusative by conjunction, and it may be in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). نُورُهُمْ يَسْعى بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ: it has been said that this is the end [of the sentence], and the meaning of وَبِأَيْمانِهِمْ is: they are given their records [in their right hands]; this meaning has been reported from Ibn ʿAbbās. يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا أَتْمِمْ لَنا نُورَنا: the doubling appears [unassimilated] because the second [mīm] is quiescent. وَاغْفِرْ لَنا: assimilation of the rāʾ into the lām is not permissible because of the trilled quality (takrīr) in it. إِنَّكَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ: the khabar of "inna"; and «كلّ», in the genitive, properly belongs at the end of the sentence, because it is an explanation (tabyīn).

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: It has been said: striving against the hypocrites is with the tongue and by withdrawing from them, and this is how one must deal with the people of sins when one cannot prevent them from them, because being at ease with them emboldens them to commit them openly; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded striving against them in this way. The root sense of "al-mujāhada" in the language is exerting one's utmost effort (al-juhd) in seeking the good pleasure of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. وَمَأْواهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ: that is, it is their abode and dwelling. وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ: that is, evil is what they arrive at: the Fire.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا امْرَأَتَ نُوحٍ وَامْرَأَتَ لُوطٍ: two objects.
كانَتا تَحْتَ عَبْدَيْنِ مِنْ عِبادِنا صالِحَيْنِ فَخانَتاهُما فَلَمْ يُغْنِيا عَنْهُما مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً: the point of this is that no one's faith, and no one's obedience, benefits anyone else, whether through kinship or otherwise, if he is disobedient to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, just as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his aunt Ṣafiyya: "I cannot avail you anything against Allah", and he said the same to Fāṭima, may Allah be pleased with her. وَقِيلَ ادْخُلَا النَّارَ مَعَ الدَّاخِلِينَ: He did not say "with those [women] who enter", because the meaning is "with the people who enter".

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: So Pharaoh's disbelief did not harm her at all. The origin [of "rabbi"] is «ربّي»; the yāʾ was dropped because the vocative is a place of omission; keeping it and giving it fatḥa are [also] permissible.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
وَمَرْيَمَ ابْنَتَ عِمْرانَ: conjoined, i.e. "and Allah set forth as an example for those who believe Maryam". ابْنَتَ: its naʿt (adjective), or, if you wish, a badal (substitute). One says "ibna" and "bint". الَّتِي أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَها فَنَفَخْنا فِيهِ مِنْ رُوحِنا: the hāʾ refers back to "al-farj". Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned two views on its meaning: one of them is that it is the opening of her garment (jayb), and the other is that it is the private part itself. The argument of whoever says it is the private part itself is "the usage of the Arabs": "aḥṣanat farjahā" in this sense. The argument of whoever says it is the opening of her garment is that the meaning of "aḥṣanat farjahā" is "she guarded the opening of her garment", so much so that قالَتْ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِالرَّحْمنِ مِنْكَ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَقِيًّا
[Maryam: 81] [Translator's note: so in the text; the verse is Maryam: 18]. As for مِنْ رُوحِنا, there are two views about it. One of them: of the spirit that is Ours and that We own, just as one says "the House of Allah". The other: "of Our spirit" means of Jibrāʾīl ﷺ; He, exalted be His praise, said: نَزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوحُ الْأَمِينُ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 193].
وَصَدَّقَتْ بِكَلِماتِ رَبِّها وَكُتُبِهِ: whoever reads it in the singular [kitābihi] says: because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); whoever reads it in the plural takes it as referring to different kinds. وَكانَتْ مِنَ الْقانِتِينَ: that is, of the devout people; the adjective was set in place of the noun it qualifies.

safi-cedvel:2-2.t:
* I'rab:
(قد) a particle of realisation (ḥarf taḥqīq); (لكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (فرض), in the sense of "prescribed"; (الواو) resumptive — or circumstantial (ḥāliyya) — and the second one is a conjunction.
The clause «قد فرض اللَّه ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «اللَّه مولاكم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: It may be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).].
The clause «هو العليم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause اللَّه مولاكم.

* Morphology:
(تحلّة): a maṣdar (verbal noun) known by hearing (samāʿī) of the quadriliteral حلّل; the regular (qiyāsī) one is تحليل.

safi-cedvel:3-3.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (إذ) an adverb of past time, in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb indicated by His words العليم الخبير, i.e. "Allah knew"; (إلى بعض) attached to (أسرّ); (الفاء) conjunction; (لمّا) an adverb in the sense of "when", containing the meaning of condition, in the position of accusative, attached to the apodosis عرّف; (به) attached to (نبّأت); (عليه) attached to (أظهره) by its being made to carry (taḍmīn) the meaning of أطلعه "informed him"; (عن بعض) attached to (أعرض); (فلمّا نبّأها به) is like فلما نبّأت به.
The clause «أسرّ النبيّ ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «نبّات به ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أظهره ...» is in the position of genitive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause نبّأت به [Note: It may be parenthetical, or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) with قد implied.].
The clause «عرّف ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أعرض ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the apodosis.
The clause «نبّأها به ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قالت ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «من أنبأك ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أنبأك هذا ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (من).
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «نبّأني العليم ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of speech.

safi-cedvel:4-5.t:
* I'rab:
(إلى اللَّه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تتوبا); (الفاء) causal (taʿlīliyya); (قد) a particle of realisation (ḥarf taḥqīq); (الواو) conjunction; (تظاهرا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), from which one of the two tāʾs has been deleted; (عليه) attached to (تظاهرا); (الفاء) causal; (هو) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is مولاه, the nominal clause being the khabar of إنّ.]; (جبريل) a mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ), whose khabar is (ظهير) [Note: Or it is conjoined to the position of إنّ and its noun — whose position is nominative — and (الملائكة) is then a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is ظهير, the clause being independent of the first and conjoined to it.]; (صالح) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to جبريل, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw, which has been deleted for lightness, in keeping with the reading in continuous recitation (waṣl); (بعد) an accusative adverb, attached to the khabar ظهير.
The clause «تتوبا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "He will accept from you both" or "you will both be accepted".
The clause «قد صغت قلوبكما ...» has no grammatical position: a causal explanation of the condition, i.e.: if you both repent to Allah — because you have both inclined with your own selves — He will accept repentance from you both.
The clause «تظاهرا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause تتوبا. The apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "he will find a helper who helps him".
The clause «إن اللَّه ... مولاه» has no grammatical position: a causal explanation of the second apodosis.
The clause «جبريل ... ظهير» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the last causal clause.
5- (طلّقكنّ) a past verb in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (أن) an infinitival and subjunctive-governing particle; (خيرا) a naʿt (adjective) of (أزواجا), accusative (manṣūb); (منكنّ) attached to (خيرا); (مسلمات ...) ḥāl (circumstantial) of (أزواجا) [Note: It has become specified by the naʿt. It may also be a second naʿt of (أزواجا), along with the rest of the other descriptions.], accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يبدله ...) is in the position of accusative as khabar of عسى.
The clause «عسى ربّه ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «طلّقكنّ ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical. The apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e.: if he divorces you, then perhaps his Lord will give him in exchange...
The clause «يبدله ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(صغت): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion on account of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the lām of the word has been deleted. Its pattern is فعت.
(ثيّبات): plural of ثيّب, a feminine generic noun (ism jins); the woman is so called because she returns (تثوب) to her parents' house. Its pattern is فيعل, and it contains iʿlāl by substitution: its original form is ثيوب — with sukūn on the yāʾ and kasra on the wāw — the wāw was changed into yāʾ and assimilated into the other yāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
The secret of the plural: in His words «قلوبكما».
The plural is used in «قلوبكما» rather than the dual, because of the dislike of two duals coming together, while the intended meaning is clear; in such cases this is more commonly used than the dual or the singular.

safi-cedvel:6-6.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين) is like يأيّها النبيّ [Note: In verse (1) of Surat al-Ṭalāq.]; (نارا) a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, governed by (قوا); (عليها) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (ملائكة); (لا) negative; (ما) an infinitival particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, with the referent pronoun omitted, i.e.: in what He commanded them.], and the second one is a relative, with the referent pronoun omitted.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما أمرهم ...) is in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) of the Name of Majesty, i.e.: they do not disobey Allah's command.
The clause «النداء ...» (the vocative) has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «قوا ...» has no grammatical position: response to the vocative.
The clause «وقودها الناس» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (نارا).
The clause «عليها ملائكة ...» is in the position of accusative as a second naʿt of (نارا).
The clause «لا يعصون ...» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt of ملائكة.
The clause «يفعلون ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause لا يعصون.
The clause «أمرهم ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «يؤمرون» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(قوا): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion in two places. The first is the fāʾ of the word, beginning from the imperfect because it fell between a yāʾ and a kasra; the deletion then extended to the imperative — as in the mithāl weak verb. The second is the lām of the word, also beginning from the imperfect, where it was attributed to the wāw of the plural; then the deletion extended to the imperative. The original form is يقيونا: the ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made quiescent and the vowel was transferred to the qāf [Note: Some said: the yāʾ was deleted because of its heaviness, then the qāf was given ḍamma to suit the wāw.]; when two quiescent letters met, the yāʾ was deleted; then the deletion carried over to the imperative, and the nūn was deleted for indeclinability (bināʾ). Its pattern is عوا.
(يعصون): it contains iʿlāl by deletion; its original form is يعصيون: the ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made quiescent and the vowel was transferred to the ṣād; when two quiescent letters met, the yāʾ was deleted, and it became يعصون. Its pattern is يفعون.

* Rhetoric:
The device of negation and affirmation (al-salb wa-l-ījāb): in His words لا يَعْصُونَ اللَّهَ ما أَمَرَهُمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ ما يُؤْمَرُونَ.
This device is building speech upon negating a thing from one aspect and affirming it from another, or commanding a thing from one aspect and forbidding it from other than that aspect.
In the noble verse, He, Mighty and Majestic, negated disobedience of those so described, and affirmed obedience for them.

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) a prohibitive, jussive-governing particle; (اليوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تعتذروا); (إنّما) the restraining particle and the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (الواو) in (تجزون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (ما) an infinitival particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of accusative, with the referent pronoun omitted.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كنتم ...) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) with a muḍāf omitted, i.e.: the recompense of what you used to...
The clause «النداء ...» (the vocative) has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Or it is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied saying, i.e.: the angels say ...].
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لا تعتذروا ...» has no grammatical position: response to the vocative.
The clause «تجزون ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «كنتم تعملون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «تعملون» is in the position of accusative as khabar (predicate) of كنتم.

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(إلى اللَّه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (توبوا); (أن) an infinitival and subjunctive-governing particle; (عنكم) attached to (يكفّر) by its being made to carry (taḍmīn) the meaning of ينزل "remove"; (الواو) conjunction in the four places; (يدخلكم) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (يكفّر); (من تحتها) attached to (تجري) with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. from beneath its trees [Note: Or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of الأنهار.]; (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يدخلكم) [Note: Or it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember".]; (لا) negative; (الذين) a relative in the position of accusative, conjoined to النبيّ [Note: Or in the position of nominative, whose khabar is the clause نورهم يسعى ...]; (معه) an accusative adverb, attached to (آمنوا); (بين) an accusative adverb, attached to (يسعى) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يسعى.]; (بأيمانهم) attached to what بين is attached to, for it is conjoined to it; (لنا) attached to (أتمم), and the second one attached to (اغفر); (على كلّ) attached to the khabar (predicate) (قدير).
The clause «النداء ...» (the vocative) has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «توبوا ...» has no grammatical position: response to the vocative.
The clause «عسى ربّكم ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يكفّر ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكفّر ...) is in the position of accusative as khabar of عسى.
The clause «يدخلكم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يكفّر.
The clause «تجري ...» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of جنّات.
The clause «لا يخزي اللَّه ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «آمنوا» (the second) has no grammatical position: ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «نورهم يسعى ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Or it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of النبيّ and الذين آمنوا معه.].
The clause «يسعى ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (نورهم).
The clause «يقولون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun in أيديهم [Note: Or it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.].
The clause «النداء ...» (the vocative) is in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أتمم ...» has no grammatical position: response to the vocative.
The clause «اغفر لنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «إنّك ... قدير» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(نصوحا): a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from the triliteral نصح ... or it is one of the intensive forms (ṣiyagh al-mubālagha). Its pattern is فعول with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī): in His words تَوْبَةً نَصُوحاً.
Repentance has been described as sincere (nuṣḥ) by way of figurative attribution, whereas sincerity is the attribute of those who repent: that they counsel themselves sincerely with repentance, and so perform it in its proper way, making amends for past failings and erasing evil deeds.

safi-cedvel:9-9.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction in the three places, and circumstantial (ḥāliyya) — or resumptive — in the fourth place. The one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "هي", i.e. Hell.
The clause «النداء ...» (the vocative) has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «جاهد ...» has no grammatical position: response to the vocative.
The clause «اغلظ ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the response to the vocative.
The clause «مأواهم جهنّم» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied causal clause, i.e.: We shall call them to account, and their refuge is Hell ...
The clause «بئس المصير» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of جهنّم, the governing factor in it being ibtidāʾ (inception as subject).].

safi-cedvel:10-12.t:
* I'rab:
(مثلا) a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), fronted; (للذين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of (مثلا) [Note: Or attached to (مثلا).]; (امرأة) a first mafʿūl bihi, postponed [Note: With a muḍāf omitted, i.e. the state of the wife.], accusative; (الواو) conjunction in both places; (تحت) an accusative adverb, attached to the khabar (predicate) of كانتا, the adverbial sense being figurative; (من عبادنا) attached to a naʿt of (عبدين); (الفاء) conjunction in both places; (عنهما) attached to (يغنيا) by its being made to carry (taḍmīn) the meaning of يدفعا "ward off"; (من الله) attached to (يغنيا) with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. from the punishment of Allah; (شيئا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar [Note: Or it is an accusative mafʿūl bihi.], i.e. anything of avail; (مع) an accusative adverb, attached to (ادخلا).
The clause «ضرب الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «كانتا تحت ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «خانتاهما ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause كانتا ...
The clause «لم يغنيا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause خانتاهما.
The clause «قيل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لم يغنيا.
The clause «ادخلا ...» is in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Note: Because it is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl) with the active verb.].
11- (الواو) conjunction in the four places; (ضرب الله ... امرأة فرعون) is like ضرب الله ... امرأة نوح; (إذ) an adverb of past time, in the position of accusative, attached to (مثلا); (ربّ) one addressed in the vocative (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, which has been deleted for lightness; (لي) attached to (ابن); (عندك) an accusative adverb, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (لي) [Note: Or to a ḥāl of (بيتا), being a naʿt placed before what it qualifies ... And (في الجنّة) may be a badal (substitute) — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — of the adverb عندك ...]; (في الجنّة) attached to a naʿt of (بيتا); (من فرعون) attached to (نجّني); (من القوم) attached to the second (نجّني) ...
The clause «ضرب الله» (the second) has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause ضرب الله (the first).
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «قالت ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «النداء وجوابه ...» (the vocative and its response) is in the position of accusative as the object of speech.
The clause «ابن لي ...» has no grammatical position: response to the vocative.
The clause «نجّني» (the first) ... has no grammatical position: conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «نجّني» (the second) ... has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause نجّني (the first).
12- (الواو) conjunction in the four places; (مريم) conjoined to (امرأة فرعون), accusative; (بنة) a badal of مريم — or ʿaṭf bayān to it — accusative; (التي) a relative in the position of accusative as a naʿt of مريم; (فيه) attached to (نفخنا), the pronoun referring to her chastity (farj) figuratively, because the breathing was into the opening of her garment; (من روحنا) attached to (نفخنا), and (من) is partitive; (بكلمات) attached to (صدّقت); (من القانتين) attached to the khabar of كانت ...
The clause «أحصنت ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative (التي).
The clause «نفخنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «صدّقت ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.: so she conceived ʿĪsā and believed in the words ...
The clause «كانت من القانتين ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause صدّقت [Note: The clause may be a ḥāl with قد implied.] ...

* Rhetoric:
1- Representation (al-tamthīl): in His words «ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا ...» — the verse.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, likened the state of the disbelievers — in that they are punished for their disbelief and their enmity towards the believers with a punishment like theirs, without leniency or favouritism, and that whatever bond of kinship by lineage or tie by marriage there was between them and the believers does not benefit them alongside their enmity, because their enmity towards him and their disbelief in Allah and His Messenger cut the ties and severed the connection, and made them further than strangers, and further still, even if the believer to whom the disbeliever is connected is a prophet among the prophets of Allah — to the state of the wife of Nūḥ and the wife of Lūṭ: when they acted hypocritically and betrayed the two messengers, the two messengers did not avail them at all against the punishment of Allah, by right of the marriage bond between them.
2- Allusion (al-taʿrīḍ): in His words «ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا» — the verse. In the striking of these two similitudes there is an allusion to the two Mothers of the Believers mentioned at the beginning of the surah and to what they had committed of backing each other against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in what he disliked, and a warning to them in the sternest and strongest way, because of the mention of disbelief in the similitude; and an indication that it was their due to be, in sincerity and in perfection in it, like these two believing women, and not to rely on their being wives of the Messenger of Allah. The allusion to Ḥafṣa is more likely, because the wife of Lūṭ disclosed his secret just as Ḥafṣa disclosed the secret of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

* Benefits:
The purity of the honour of the prophets ...
In this verse Allah struck a similitude: that the corrupt, disobedient disbeliever is not benefited by the righteousness of another, even if he were a prophet. The wife of Nūḥ, whose name was Wāʿila — and it was said: Wālʿa — and the wife of Lūṭ, whose name was Wāhila — and it was said: Wālha — were wives of two righteous servants who were prophets, namely Nūḥ and Lūṭ, upon them be blessings and peace (فخانتاهما). Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: The wife of a prophet never committed fornication; their betrayal was only that they were upon a religion other than theirs. The wife of Nūḥ used to say to people: He is mad, and when anyone believed in him she would inform the tyrants of her people. As for the wife of Lūṭ, she used to direct her people to his guests: when a guest came to him at night she would light a fire, and when a guest came to him by day she would make smoke, to let her people know of that. Therefore the scholars are unanimous on the purity of the honour of the prophets, and they said: if the wife of a prophet persists in disbelief, this does not impugn his honour and his protection (ʿiṣma); but if she were to commit fornication, this would not accord with the protection of the prophets and their purity, for their honour is safeguarded from fornication, and so that never occurs among their women.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {ضَرَبَ الله مَثَلاً} to the end: the discussion of «ضَرَبَ» together with «المثل» has already preceded — whether it means صَيَّر ("to make") or not, and how what follows it is put in the accusative — in Sūrat al-Naḥl, which makes repeating it here unnecessary.
His saying: {كَانَتَا تَحْتَ عَبْدَيْنِ} is a resumptive (mustaʾnafa) clause, as if explicative (mufassira) of the striking of the parable. He did not bring their pronoun, so as to say "تحتهما", i.e. under Nūḥ and Lūṭ, because of what was intended of honouring them with these noble descriptions:
4280 - لا تَدْعُني إلاَّ ب «يا عبدَها» ... فإنَّه أشرفُ أسمائي
(Do not call me except by "O her servant", for it is the noblest of my names.) — and so as to describe them with the most exalted of attributes, which is righteousness.
His saying: {فَلَمْ يُغْنِيا}: the majority read it with the yāʾ from below, i.e. Nūḥ and Lūṭ did not avail their two wives anything at all against the punishment of Allah.
Mubashshir ibn ʿUbayd read «تُغْنِيا» with the tāʾ from above, i.e. so the two women did not avail themselves. There is a difficulty in it, since it entails that the verb of an attached latent pronoun passes over (taʿaddī) to its own attached pronoun outside the excepted places. The answer is that «عَنْ» here is a noun, as it is in his saying:
4281 - دَعْ عنك نَهْباً صِيْحَ في حَجَراتِهِ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Leave aside a plunder cried out over in its sides …)
This has already been presented to you, together with the objection to it from His saying: {وهزى إِلَيْكِ} [Maryam: 25] and {واضمم إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 32], and the answer given there.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {إِذْ قَالَتْ}: it is accusative (manṣūb) by «ضَرَبَ», even though the appearance of the striking [of the parable] is later; and it may be put in the accusative by «المَثَل».
His saying: {عِندَكَ}: it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «ابنِ», or attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «بيتاً»: it was its naʿt (adjective), and when it was placed first it was put in the accusative as a ḥāl. And «في الجنة» is either attached to «ابْنِ» or to an omitted element as a naʿt of «بيتاً».

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {وَمَرْيَمَ}: it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «امرأةَ فرعونَ»: Allah the Exalted struck the parable for the unbelievers with two women and for the believers with two women. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«ومريم», i.e. and mention Maryam. And it was said: and the parable of Maryam." End of quote. There is no need for this, given the evident meaning that I have mentioned.
The majority read «ابنةَ» with the tāʾ in the accusative. Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī read it with a quiescent hāʾ in continuous recitation, treating continuation like pausing. The majority also read «فَنَفَخْنا فيه», i.e. into the private part; and ʿAbd Allāh read «فيها», i.e. into her as a whole. Something similar has preceded in al-Anbiyāʾ.
The majority also read «وصَدَّقَتْ» with the dāl doubled. Yaʿqūb, Qatāda, Abū Mijlaz and ʿĀṣim in one transmission read it with it undoubled, i.e. she was truthful in what she reported of the matter of ʿĪsā, peace be upon him. The majority read «بكلمات» as a plural; al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and al-Jaḥdarī read «بكلمة» in the singular. It was said: what is meant by it is ʿĪsā, because he is the Word of Allah. The disagreement over «وكتبه» has preceded at the end of al-Baqara. Abū Rajāʾ read «وكُتْبِه» with a quiescent tāʾ, which is a good lightening, and «وكَتْبِه» with the kāf vowelled with fatḥa was reported from him. Abū al-Faḍl said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in the place of the noun, meaning: and what He wrote (maktūbihi).
His saying: {مِنَ القانتين}: two views are permissible regarding «مِن». The first: that it is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya). The second: that it is partitive (li-l-tabʿīḍ). Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned both, saying: "«مِنْ» is partitive. It may also be for the beginning of the extent, in the sense that she was born of the devoutly obedient (al-qānitīn), since she was of the descendants of Hārūn, the brother of Mūsā, peace be upon them both." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it said «من القانتين» in the masculine? I say: because devout obedience (al-qunūt) is a quality that includes whoever was devoutly obedient of both sexes, so he gave preponderance to its males over its females."

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {تَبْتَغِي}: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «تُحَرِّم», that is: "why do you forbid, seeking by it the good pleasure of your wives?" It may be an explanation of «تُحَرِّمُ», and it may be resumptive, in which case it is an answer to the question. «مَرْضاة» is a noun of verbal action (ism maṣdar), which is الرِّضا, and its original is مَرْضَوَة, as has been given; and the maṣdar here is annexed (muḍāf), either to the object or to the agent, that is: "that you please your wives" or "that they be pleased".

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {تَحِلَّةَ}: the maṣdar of تَحَلَّل with shadda, and it is like تَكْرِمَة; these two are not regular, for the regular maṣdar of faʿʿala is taf ʿīl when it is sound and not hamzated. As for those whose lām is weak, such as زَكَّى, and the hamzated, such as نَبَّأ, their maṣdar is tafʿila, such as تَزْكية and تَنْبِئة; although the taf ʿīl in full has come in the weak [verb] too, as in his saying:
4276 - باتَتْ تُنَزِّي دَلْوَها تَنْزِيَّا ...
(She spent the night making her bucket leap, leaping...)
Its original is تَحْلِلَه like تكْرِمة, so it was assimilated. And its accusative is as a direct object.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {وَإِذَ أَسَرَّ}: the governor in it is «اذكُرْ» ("remember"), so it is a direct object, not an adverbial.
His saying: {فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَتْ بِهِ}: the basic rule for نَبَّأ, أنبأ, أخبر, خبَّر and حَدَّث is that they are transitive to two objects, to the first by themselves and to the second by a preposition; sometimes the preposition is omitted for lightness, and sometimes the first is omitted because it is indicated. All three usages occur in these verses. His saying {فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَتْ بِهِ} is transitive to two, the first of which is omitted and the second is genitive with the bāʾ, that is: "she informed another of it"; and His saying {فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَهَا بِهِ} mentions both; and His saying {مَنْ أَنبَأَكَ هذا} mentions both and omits the preposition.
His saying: {عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ}: al-Kisāʾī read it with a light rāʾ; the others with shadda. With the shadda the first object is omitted, that is: "he made her know part of it", that is, he made her acquainted with it as a matter of the unseen, and turned away from part out of generosity and forbearance on his part. As for the light form, its meaning is: he requited part of it and turned away from part. In the exegesis: he confided something to Ḥafṣa, and she told another about it, so he divorced her, as requital for part of it, and did not hold her to account for the rest; and this is of the kind of His saying {وَمَا تَفْعَلُواْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ يَعْلَمْهُ الله} [al-Baqara: 197], that is, "He will requite you for it", and His saying {أولئك الذين يَعْلَمُ الله مَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 63]. We are compelled to this interpretation only because Allah the Exalted had made him aware of all that she informed another of, as in the saying of the Exalted {وَأَظْهَرَهُ الله عَلَيْهِ}. ʿIkrima read «عَرَّاف» with an alif after the rāʾ, and it was explained as a lengthening, as in his saying:
4277 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . من العَقْرابِ ... الشائلاتِ عُقَدَ الأذْنَابِ
(... of the scorpions, those that raise the knots of their tails.)
It was also said: it is a Yemeni dialect; they say «عَرَافَ زيدٌ عمراً», that is, he knew him. When these five verbs are made to imply the sense of "to inform" (aʿlama), they become transitive to three. Al-Fārisī said: "They become transitive by the hamza or the doubling," and this is a mistake, since it requires that before the doubling and the hamza they were transitive to two, and acquired a third by the hamza or the doubling; and the matter is not so, by agreement.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {إِن تَتُوبَآ}: a condition, and there are two possibilities regarding its apodosis. The first is His saying «فقد صَغَتْ», and the meaning: "If you two repent, then what makes repentance obligatory has occurred from you, namely the inclining of your hearts away from what is obligatory, in opposing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in loving what he loves and disliking what he dislikes." صَغَتْ means "inclined", and the reading of Ibn Masʿūd «فقد راغَتْ» points to it. The second is that the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being: "then that is obligatory upon you", or "then Allah will turn to you"; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. He said: "What is omitted is indicated by «فقد صَغَتْ», because the leaning of the heart to that is a sin." What he said there is no need for, and it is as if he claimed that the inclining of the heart is a sin, so how could it be good for it to be an apodosis? He overlooked the meaning I mentioned in showing its soundness as an apodosis. And «قلوبُكما» is among the most eloquent speech, where the plural is put in the place of the dual, finding two successive duals heavy had it been said «قلباكما». The treatment of this has been given in the verse of theft in [Sūrat] al-Māʾida, with the conditions of the question and what the people differed on. An instance of the dual's occurring is his saying:
4278 - فتخالَسا نَفْسَيْهما بنوافِذٍ ... كنوافِذِ العُبْطِ التي لا تُرْقَعُ
(So the two snatched each other's souls with piercing wounds, like the piercing wounds of fresh gashes that are not patched.)
The best in this chapter is the plural, then the singular, then the dual. Ibn ʿUṣfūr said: "The singular is not permissible except in necessity, as in his saying:
4279 - حمامةَ بَطْنِ الواديَيْنِ تَرَنَّمي ... سَقاكِ مِنْ الغُرِّ الغوادِي مَطيرُها
(O dove of the middle of the two valleys, sing; may the bright morning clouds' rain water you.)
The Shaykh followed him, and held Ibn Mālik mistaken in making it better than the dual. It is not a mistake, for the reason he gave, which is the dislike of two duals in succession when there is no fear of confusion.
And His saying {إِن تَتُوبَآ} contains an iltifāt (shift of person) from the third person to the second; and what is meant are the two Mothers of the Believers, the daughters of the two Shaykhs, ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa, may Allah be pleased with them and with their fathers.
His saying: {وَإِن تَظَاهَرَا}: its original is تتظاهرا, and it was assimilated; this is the reading of the majority. ʿIkrima read «تتظاهرا» in the original form. Al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, and Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim in one transmission from them, read it with shadda on the ẓāʾ and the hāʾ without an alif, and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission «تظاهرا» with the ẓāʾ and the hāʾ lightened, one of the two tāʾs being dropped. All have the meaning of mutual assistance, from al-ẓahr (the back), because it is the strongest and most important of a person's limbs.
His saying: {هُوَ مَوْلاَهُ}: «هو» may be a separator (faṣl) and «مَوْلاه» the khabar; or it may be a mubtadaʾ with «مَوْلاه» its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «إنَّ».
His saying: {وَجِبْرِيلُ}: it may be conjoined to the Name of Allah the Exalted, and made nominative with regard to the position of the noun of «إنَّ», and that after it has completed its khabar, and you know the positions of the people on that; and then «جبريلُ» and what follows enter into the guardianship of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Jibrīl is a supporter of him by his inclusion in the generality of the angels, and «الملائكة» is a mubtadaʾ and «ظهيرٌ» its khabar, put in the singular because it is on the pattern faʿīl. It is also possible that the speech is complete at His saying «مَوْلاه», and «جبريل» is a mubtadaʾ and what follows is conjoined to it, and «ظهيرٌ» is the khabar of all of them; so guardianship is restricted to Allah, and Jibrīl is mentioned twice in assistance: once by explicit mention, and once by inclusion in the generality of the angels. This is the reverse of what is in [Sūrat] al-Baqara of His saying {مَن كَانَ عَدُوّاً للَّهِ وملائكته وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ}, where the particular was mentioned after the general to honour it; and here the general is mentioned after the particular. The people mentioned only the first division.
And His saying {وَصَالِحُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ}: the apparent sense is that it is singular, and for that reason it was written with the ḥāʾ without a plural wāw. They allowed that it be a plural with wāw and nūn, the nūn dropped for iḍāfa, and written without a wāw out of regard for its pronunciation, because the wāw drops owing to the meeting of two quiescent letters, as in {وَيَمْحُ الله الباطل} [al-Shūrā: 24], {يَدْعُ الداع} and {سَنَدْعُ الزبانية} [al-ʿAlaq: 18] and others. Like this is what came in the ḥadīth: «أهلُ القرآن أهلُ الله وخاصَّتُه». They said: it may be a singular, and it may be a plural, as in His saying {شَغَلَتْنَآ أَمْوَالُنَا وَأَهْلُونَا} [al-Fatḥ: 11]; and the wāw is dropped owing to the meeting of two quiescent letters in pronunciation; so when this is written, it is better to write it with the wāw for this purpose, and there is no necessity to drop it, as has passed in the orthography.
Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed that «جبريلُ» be conjoined to the pronoun in «مَوْلاه», meaning the latent one, and then the separation by the genitive pronoun is enough to permit the conjunction to it. He also allowed that it be a mubtadaʾ, with «صالحُ» conjoined to it, and the khabar omitted, that is: "his protectors".

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {إِن طَلَّقَكُنَّ}: a condition, parenthetical between the noun of ʿasā and its khabar; its apodosis is omitted or fronted, that is: "if he divorces you, perhaps...". Abū ʿAmr assimilated the qāf into the kāf, in the view of some, who said: "That is preferable to «يَرْزُقكم» and the like, because of the heaviness of the feminine."
«مُسْلماتٍ» to the end: it is either a naʿt, or a ḥāl, or accusative as ikhtiṣāṣ. The two readings of {يُبْدِلَهُ}, light and with shadda, were given in [Sūrat] al-Kahf. ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid read «سَيِّحاتٍ». The wāw was put between «ثَيِّبات» and «أَبْكاراً» only because the two descriptions are mutually exclusive, unlike the other qualities. And ثَيِّبات and the like is not regular, because it is a feminine generic noun, so one does not say نساء خَوْدات, nor رأيت عِيْنات.
الثَّيِّب has the pattern fayʿil, from ثاب يثوب, meaning "to return", as if she had returned after the loss of her virginity; its original is ثَيْوِب, like سَيِّد and مَيِّت, whose originals are سَيْوِد and مَيْوِت, and they underwent the well-known weakening (iʿlāl).

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {قوا أَنفُسَكُمْ}: an imperative from الوِقاية, so its pattern is «عُوا», because the fāʾ was dropped as it falls in the imperfect between a yāʾ and a kasra, and this is carried over to it; and the lām was dropped by analogy to the jussive. To explain: its original is اِوْقِيُوا like اضْرِبوا, so the wāw which is the fāʾ was dropped for the reason given; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was found heavy and dropped; two quiescent letters met, so the yāʾ was dropped and what is before the wāw given a ḍamma so that it is sound. This is the reasoning of the Basrans. Makkī reported from the Kufans that the dropping in their view is to distinguish the transitive from the intransitive, so the wāw that is the fāʾ was dropped in يَقي and يَعِدُ because they are transitive, and not dropped from يَوْجَل because it is intransitive. He said: "Against them stands يَرِمُ, which is intransitive, and yet they dropped its fāʾ." I say: there is room for objection in this, because in يَوْجَل the wāw does not fall between a yāʾ and a kasra, neither overt nor latent; and I said "nor latent" to guard against يَضَعُ, يَسَعُ and يَهَبُ.
And «ناراً» is the second object. {وَقُودُهَا الناس} is a ṣifa of «ناراً», and likewise «عليها ملائكةٌ». It is also possible that the qualifier is «عليها» alone, with «ملائكةٌ» its agent. It is possible too that it is a ḥāl, being specified by the first qualifier, and likewise {لاَّ يَعْصُونَ الله}.
Some read «وأَهْلوكم», and it was explained as a conjunction to the nominative pronoun in «قُوا», and the separation by the object permitted that. Al-Zamakhsharī said, after mentioning the reading and its explanation: "If you ask: is the implied form not: 'protect yourselves, and let your families protect yourselves'? I say: no. Rather, the conjoined element in the implied form is accompanied by the wāw, and «أنفسَكم» comes after it, as if it were said: 'Protect, you and your families, yourselves'; since you combined the one addressed with the absent, you gave precedence to the former and made the pronoun of both together in the wording of the one addressed." The disagreement about the wāw of «وقود», with ḍamma or fatḥa, was given in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.
His saying: {مَآ أَمَرَهُمْ}: «ما» may be in the sense of «الذي», with the returning pronoun omitted, that is "what He commanded them", the original being "with which (bihi)". It is not said: how can the genitive returning pronoun be omitted when the relative noun is not governed by a like preposition? Because the dropping of this particle is regular, so it was dropped only when [the pronoun] was accusative. It may also be a maṣdar particle, its position being a badal ishtimāl (inclusion substitute) from the Name of Allah, as if it were said: "they do not disobey His command".
And His saying {وَيَفْعَلُونَ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: are the two clauses not of one meaning? I say: no; for the first means that they accept His commands and hold to them, and the second means that they carry out what they are commanded, not being slow in it nor hesitating in it."

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {نَّصُوحاً}: the majority read it with fatḥa on the nūn, and it is a form of exaggeration (ṣīghat mubālagha), with advising ascribed to it figuratively; it is from نَصَح الثوبَ, meaning "he sewed it", as if the repentant mends what he tore by disobedience. It was also said: from their saying «عسلٌ ناصِح», meaning "pure honey". Abū Bakr read it with ḍamma on the nūn, which is a maṣdar of نَصَحَ; one says نَصَحَ نُصْحاً and نُصوحاً, like كَفَرَ كُفْراً and كُفوراً, and شَكَر شُكراً and شُكوراً. There are several possibilities concerning its accusative. The first is that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), that is: "for the sake of the sincere counsel whose benefit accrues to you." The second is that it is an emphatic maṣdar of an omitted verb, that is: "He counsels them in counsel." The third is that it is a ṣifa of it, either by way of exaggeration, on the footing that it is the maṣdar itself, or on an omitted muḍāf, that is: "possessing sincere counsel".
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «تَوْباً» without the tāʾ [of feminine ending].
His saying: {وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ}: the reading of the majority is the accusative by ʿaṭf on «يُكَفِّر»; Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «يُكَفِّرْ» with sukūn on the rāʾ, which may be from treating what is separate as attached, so the kasra was made quiescent, because from the whole «يُكَفِّرَ عنكم» it is imagined to be like نِطَع and قِمَع, of which one says نِطْع and قِمْع. It may also be a conjunction on the position of «عسى أَنْ يُكَفِّر», as if it were said: "Repent: it will necessitate the expiation of your misdeeds, and He will admit you"; al-Zamakhsharī said this. He means that «عسى» is in the position of jussive as the answer to the command, because if an imperfect were to occupy its place it would be jussive, as al-Zamakhsharī illustrated; and there is room for objection in it, because we do not concede that «عسى» is an apodosis, and it does not occur as an apodosis because it is for expressing a wish (inshāʾ).
His saying: {يَوْمَ لاَ يُخْزِى}: accusative by «يُدْخلكم» or by an implied «اذكُرْ».
His saying: {والذين آمَنُواْ}: two possibilities. The first is that it is conjoined to «النبيَّ» [that is]: "and does not disgrace those who believe." On this «نُورُهم يسعى» is resumptive or a ḥāl. The second is that it is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is «نورُهم يَسْعى», and «يقولون» a second khabar or a ḥāl. The i'rāb of clauses like these was given in [Sūrat] al-Ḥadīd, so you should consider it. The i'rāb of what follows it was given in [Sūrat] Barāʾa.
Abū Ḥaywa and Sahl al-Fahmī read «وبإيمانهم» with kasra on the hamza, and this was given in [Sūrat] al-Ḥadīd.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكَ تَبْتَغِي مَرْضَاةَ أَزْوَاجِكَ. . . (١))
His saying (تَبْتَغِي): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «تُحَرِّمُ», and it may be resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا امْرَأَةَ نُوحٍ وَامْرَأَةَ لُوطٍ كَانَتَا تَحْتَ عَبْدَيْنِ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا صَالِحَيْنِ فَخَانَتَاهُمَا فَلَمْ يُغْنِيَا عَنْهُمَا مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا وَقِيلَ ادْخُلَا النَّارَ مَعَ الدَّاخِلِينَ (١٠))
His saying (اِمْرَأَةَ نُوحٍ وَامْرَأَةَ لُوطٍ), i.e. "the likeness of the wife of Nūḥ"; this has been mentioned in Yā Sīn and elsewhere. And (كَانَتَا) is resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا امْرَأَةَ فِرْعَوْنَ إِذْ قَالَتْ رَبِّ ابْنِ لِي عِنْدَكَ بَيْتًا فِي الْجَنَّةِ وَنَجِّنِي مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ وَعَمَلِهِ وَنَجِّنِي مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ (١١))
And (إِذْ قَالَتْ): what governs إِذْ is الْمَثَل (the likeness). And (عِنْدَكَ) may be an adverb (ẓarf) for ابْنِ, and may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «بَيْتًا».

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَرْيَمَ ابْنَتَ عِمْرَانَ الَّتِي أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهِ مِنْ رُوحِنَا. . . (١٢))
His saying (وَمَرْيَمَ), i.e. "and remember مَرْيَمَ", or "and the likeness of مَرْيَمَ". And (فِيهِ): the hāʾ refers back to الْفَرْج. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَدْ فَرَضَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ تَحِلَّةَ أَيْمَانِكُمْ. . . (٢))
The origin of (تَحِلَّةَ) is تَحْلِلَة; the first [lām] was made vowelless and assimilated.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ أَسَرَّ النَّبِيُّ إِلَى بَعْضِ أَزْوَاجِهِ حَدِيثًا فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَتْ بِهِ وَأَظْهَرَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ وَأَعْرَضَ عَنْ بَعْضٍ فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَهَا بِهِ قَالَتْ مَنْ أَنْبَأَكَ هَذَا قَالَ نَبَّأَنِيَ الْعَلِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ (٣))
And (إِذْ) is in the position of the accusative, governed by an implied "remember" (اذْكُرْ).
His saying (عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ): whoever reads it with a doubled [rāʾ] makes it transitive to two objects, the second being omitted, i.e. "he made known part of it to one of his wives". Whoever reads it light [عَرَفَ] takes it in the sense of requital, not of actual knowing, because he knew all of it; it is like His saying (وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ) and similar verses, i.e. "He will requite you for your deeds".

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنْ تَتُوبَا إِلَى اللَّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا وَإِنْ تَظَاهَرَا عَلَيْهِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ مَوْلَاهُ وَجِبْرِيلُ وَصَالِحُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ (٤))
His saying (إِنْ تَتُوبَا): the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted; its implied form is "then that is incumbent upon you both", or "Allah will turn to you both in forgiveness". The omitted element is indicated by (فَقَدْ صَغَتْ), because the heart's inclining towards that is a sin.
His saying (قُلُوبُكُمَا): it is plural although they are two, because every person has [only one] heart; and for a thing of which a person has only one, it is permissible to express two of them with the plural form, and permissible to use the dual form.
It is also said: the reason is that the dual is a plural.
His saying (هُوَ مَوْلَاهُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) [together form] the khabar of إِنَّ. «هُوَ» may also be a separating pronoun (faṣl). As for «جِبْرِيلُ وَصَالِحُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ», there are two views. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted, i.e. "are his protectors"; or it is conjoined to the pronoun in مَوْلَاهُ, or to the [position of the] mubtadaʾ in meaning.
The second: it is a mubtadaʾ, «الْمَلَائِكَةُ» is conjoined to it, and «ظَهِيرٌ» is the khabar of them all; it is a singular with a plural meaning, i.e. ظُهَرَاءُ (helpers).

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (عَسَى رَبُّهُ إِنْ طَلَّقَكُنَّ أَنْ يُبْدِلَهُ أَزْوَاجًا خَيْرًا مِنْكُنَّ مُسْلِمَاتٍ مُؤْمِنَاتٍ قَانِتَاتٍ تَائِبَاتٍ عَابِدَاتٍ سَائِحَاتٍ ثَيِّبَاتٍ وَأَبْكَارًا (٥))
And (مُسْلِمَاتٍ) is another naʿt (adjective), and the attributes after it likewise.
As for the wāw in His saying (وَأَبْكَارًا), it is indispensable, because the meaning is that some of them are previously married and some of them virgins.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَارًا وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ وَالْحِجَارَةُ عَلَيْهَا مَلَائِكَةٌ غِلَاظٌ شِدَادٌ لَا يَعْصُونَ اللَّهَ مَا أَمَرَهُمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ مَا يُؤْمَرُونَ (٦))
His saying (قُوا): in this verb [what remains] is its middle radical, because its first and last radicals are weak. The wāw was dropped in the imperfect because it fell between an open yāʾ and a kasra, and the imperative is built on the imperfect.
His saying (لَا يَعْصُونَ اللَّهَ): it is in the position of the nominative, as a naʿt (adjective).
«[Translator's note: the source reads «فِي هَذَا الْفِعْلِ عَيْنُهُ», apparently defective for "nothing remains of this verb but its middle radical"; the bracketed words are added.]»

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا تُوبُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ تَوْبَةً نَصُوحًا عَسَى رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ يُكَفِّرَ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ يَوْمَ لَا يُخْزِي اللَّهُ النَّبِيَّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ نُورُهُمْ يَسْعَى بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمَانِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا إِنَّكَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (٨))
His saying (تَوْبَةً نَصُوحًا) is read with fatḥa on the nūn; it is said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); and it is also said: it is an active participle, i.e. "sincere (نَاصِحَة)", figuratively. It is also read with ḍamma on it [نُصُوحًا], and then it is only a maṣdar, like الْقُعُود.
His saying (يَقُولُونَ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it may be resumptive.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Taḥrīm (The Prohibition)
Medinan
﷽
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ ما أحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكَ تَبْتَغِي مَرْضاتَ أزْواجِكَ واللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ means: Allah has forgiven you that prohibition. It has come in the exegesis that the Prophet ﷺ drank honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, and ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa agreed to say to him: "We smell on you the odour of maghāfīr." ”اَلْمَغافِيرُ“ is a gum with an altered smell; and it is said in the exegesis that it is a herb. When he came to each of them, she said to him: "I smell on you the odour of maghāfīr." So the Prophet ﷺ forbade himself the drinking of honey; and it is said that he swore to that. And it has come in the exegesis — and this is the more widely held — that the Prophet ﷺ «was alone, on a day belonging to ʿĀʾisha, with his slave-girl, the mother of Ibrāhīm, who was called "Māriya the Copt." Ḥafṣa came upon that, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: "Do not inform ʿĀʾisha of that." She said to him: "I will not." And he forbade Māriya to himself — and it is said that he also swore along with that. Then Ḥafṣa informed ʿĀʾisha of the news and asked her to keep it secret; and Allah acquainted His Prophet with that, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَإذْ أسَرَّ النَّبِيُّ إلى بَعْضِ أزْواجِهِ حَدِيثًا﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3]», meaning Ḥafṣa. The position of ”إذْ“ is accusative, as though He said: "And remember when the Prophet confided a matter to one of his wives," meaning Ḥafṣa. ﴿فَلَمّا نَبَّأتْ بِهِ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3] means: when she told ʿĀʾisha of it.

﴿وَأظْهَرَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ وأعْرَضَ عَنْ بَعْضٍ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3] — it was also read ”عَرَفَ بَعْضَهُ“, with the rāʾ undoubled. And Allah made known that the prohibition, according to this exegesis, does not make (the thing) forbidden, and He said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ ما أحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكَ تَبْتَغِي مَرْضاتَ أزْواجِكَ﴾. So Allah did not grant His Prophet the right to forbid anything except what Allah has forbidden; and according to both of these exegeses no one may forbid what Allah has made lawful. Then Allah said: ﴿قَدْ فَرَضَ اللَّهُ لَكم تَحِلَّةَ أيْمانِكُمْ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 2], meaning the expiation, because it has been transmitted that he swore along with that prohibition; and some said the expiation is the expiation for the prohibition (itself). As for ﴿عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3], its interpretation is that he made Ḥafṣa aware of part of it. ﴿وَأعْرَضَ عَنْ بَعْضٍ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3]: it has come in the exegesis that when he forbade Māriya (to himself), he told Ḥafṣa that after him Abū Bakr and ʿUmar would rule; so he made her aware of part of the news she had divulged and turned away from part. For the Prophet ﷺ had made known everything he had confided [Translator's note: so printed (عَرَّفَ); the argument seems to require "knew" (عَرَفَ)], and turning away can only be from what is known. The interpretation of this in the language is good and clear: the meaning of ﴿عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3] is "he requited (her) for it," as you say to someone you are threatening: "I know what you did, I am aware of what you have done," its meaning being "so I will requite you for it," not that you intend merely that you know. Like it is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَما تَفْعَلُوا مِن خَيْرٍ يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Baqara: 197], whose interpretation is: Allah knows it and requites it — for Allah knows everything that is done. Like it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ ما في قُلُوبِهِمْ فَأعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 63], while Allah knows what is in the hearts of all creatures. And like it is His saying: ﴿فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ﴾ [al-Zalzala: 7]: the point is not that he sees what he did; he only sees the recompense of what he did. It is said that the Prophet ﷺ divorced Ḥafṣa with a single pronouncement, and that was her recompense in his view; that is the interpretation of ﴿عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ وأعْرَضَ عَنْ بَعْضٍ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 3], i.e. he requited (her) for part of the matter. Ḥafṣa was much given to fasting and to standing in prayer at night, so Allah the Exalted commanded him to take her back, and he took her back.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿إنْ تَتُوبا إلى اللَّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُما﴾ — He means by it ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa. The meaning of ﴿صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُما﴾ is: your hearts have swerved and deviated from truthfulness.

His saying: ﴿وَإنْ تَظاهَرا عَلَيْهِ فَإنَّ اللَّهَ هو مَوْلاهُ﴾ means: (if) you two support one another against him, then Allah is his protector (mawlā), i.e. He undertakes his support. ﴿وَجِبْرِيلُ وصالِحُ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that "the righteous of the believers" are Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; it has also come in the exegesis that the righteous of the believers is ʿUmar; and it is said that the righteous of the believers are the best of the Muslims. ”صالِحُ“ here stands for the plural, as you say: "The good one among people does this," meaning every good person. ﴿والمَلائِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ﴾ — in the sense of ”ظُهَراءُ“ (supporters), i.e. the angels too are helpers of the Prophet ﷺ.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿عَسى رَبُّهُ إنْ طَلَّقَكُنَّ أنْ يُبْدِلَهُ أزْواجًا خَيْرًا مِنكُنَّ مُسْلِماتٍ﴾ — it was also read ”يُبَدِّلَهُ“, with a doubled dāl and a fatḥa on the bāʾ; ”يُبَدِّلَهُ“ is for intensiveness. Both are good, and it has been read so.

His saying: ﴿قانِتاتٍ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis: obedient. ”اَلْقُنُوتُ“ is performing what brings one near to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿سائِحاتٍ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis from the Prophet ﷺ «that the sāʾiḥūn are those who fast», and this is among what is in the earlier scriptures. The lexicographers said: the one fasting was only called ”سائِحٌ“ (a wanderer) because the one who wanders is devoted to worship and has no provisions with him, so when he finds provisions he eats; and the one fasting likewise spends the day without eating anything. Because of his resemblance to him he was called ”سائِحًا“.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قُوا أنْفُسَكم وأهْلِيكم نارًا﴾ means: hold yourselves and your families to what brings one near to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and keep yourselves and your families away from acts of disobedience. The meaning of ﴿قُوا أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ is: guard (waqqū) yourselves. It has come in the exegesis: "May Allah have mercy on a man who says: 'O my family, your prayer, your fasting, your poor, your orphan, your neighbours!'" — meaning: keep to and preserve your prayer and these things mentioned; fulfil Allah's obligation in them. And in the hadith: «"Perhaps Allah will gather them with him in Paradise."»

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَقُودُها النّاسُ والحِجارَةُ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that they are stones of sulphur. ”اَلْوَقُودُ“, with a fatḥa on the wāw, is that with which fire is kindled, firewood and the like; one says ”وَقَدْتُ النّارَ، وُقُودًا“ (I kindled the fire), with a ḍamma on the wāw.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا تُوبُوا إلى اللَّهِ تَوْبَةً نَصُوحًا﴾ — with a fatḥa on the nūn; it is also read ”نُصُوحًا“ with a ḍamma on the nūn. Whoever gives the fatḥa takes it as a naʿt (adjective) of the repentance, meaning "a repentance consummate in sincerity"; ”فَعُولٌ“ is one of the agent forms used for intensiveness in description: you say "a man patient (ṣabūr) and grateful (shakūr)" and "a sincere repentance (tawba naṣūḥ)." Whoever read ”نُصُوحًا“ with a ḍamma on the nūn, its meaning is "they are sincere in this with sincerity (nuṣūḥ)"; one says ”نَصَحْتُ لَهُ نُصْحًا، ونِصاحَةً، ونُصُوحًا“ (I was sincere to him).

It has come in the exegesis that the sincere repentance is that after which the penitent does not return to the sin; and some of them said: that with which he does not intend to return to the sin.

His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ لا يُخْزِي اللَّهُ النَّبِيَّ والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ﴾ — ”يَوْمَ“ is accusative through His saying: ﴿عَسى رَبُّكم أنْ يُكَفِّرَ عَنْكم سَيِّئاتِكم ويُدْخِلَكم جَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ يَوْمَ لا يُخْزِي اللَّهُ النَّبِيَّ﴾, i.e. on that day. The reading is the accusative in His saying ﴿وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ﴾, conjoined to ﴿أنْ يُكَفِّرَ﴾; had it been read with the jussive, that would be a valid way, construed on the position of ﴿عَسى رَبُّكم أنْ يُكَفِّرَ عَنْكم سَيِّئاتِكُمْ﴾, because ”عَسى“ from Allah is binding. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَإنِّي لَغَفّارٌ لِمَن تابَ وآمَنَ وعَمِلَ صالِحًا ثُمَّ اهْتَدى﴾ [Ṭāhā: 82]. And His saying: ﴿نُورُهم يَسْعى بَيْنَ أيْدِيهِمْ وبِأيْمانِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا أتْمِمْ لَنا نُورَنا﴾ means: when the believers see the light of the hypocrites being extinguished, they ask Allah to perfect their light for them.

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلا لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا امْرَأتَ نُوحٍ وامْرَأتَ لُوطٍ كانَتا تَحْتَ عَبْدَيْنِ مِن عِبادِنا صالِحَيْنِ فَخانَتاهُما فَلَمْ يُغْنِيا عَنْهُما مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا﴾ — Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that the prophets avail nothing for one who commits acts of disobedience. It has come in the exegesis that their betrayal was not in harlotry, because Allah does not afflict the prophets with corruption in their wives. It is said that the betrayal of Lūṭ's wife was that she used to point out the guests, and the betrayal of Nūḥ's wife was that she used to say he was mad — Allah bless him and all His prophets. Whoever claims otherwise is mistaken; for some of those who interpreted His saying ﴿يا نُوحُ إنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِن أهْلِكَ إنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صالِحٍ﴾ [Hūd: 46] inclined to a kind of corruption. The reading here is ”عَمِلَ غَيْرَ صالِحٍ“ and ﴿عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صالِحٍ﴾ [Hūd: 46], and both come back to one meaning: the interpretation of ﴿إنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صالِحٍ﴾ [Hūd: 46] is "he is one of unrighteous deeds." Whoever disbelieves, his kinship with his believing family is cut off: he does not inherit from them, nor do they inherit from him.

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا امْرَأتَ فِرْعَوْنَ إذْ قالَتْ رَبِّ ابْنِ لِي عِنْدَكَ بَيْتًا في الجَنَّةِ ونَجِّنِي مِن فِرْعَوْنَ وعَمَلِهِ﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that Pharaoh drove four stakes for her, bound her body and her legs, placed a millstone on her chest and put her in the sun; and that Allah gave her relief, and she saw her house in Paradise. It has also come in the exegesis that the angels used to shade her from the sun with their wings.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَرْيَمَ ابْنَتَ عِمْرانَ الَّتِي أحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَها فَنَفَخْنا فِيهِ مِن رُوحِنا وصَدَّقَتْ بِكَلِماتِ رَبِّها وكُتُبِهِ﴾ — it was also read ”وَكِتابِهِ“. ﴿أحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَها﴾: it has come in the exegesis that what is meant by it is the opening of her garment. The Arabs say of a chaste man: "He is clean of garment" and "He is good of waistband (ḥujza)," meaning that he is chaste. They recited the verse of al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī:
؎رِقاقُ النِّعالِ طَيِّبٌ حُجُزاتُهم ∗∗∗ يُحَيُّونَ بِالرَّيْحانِ يَوْمَ السَّباسِبِ
(Fine of sandals, good of waistbands, they are greeted with sweet basil on the day of al-Sabāsib.)
They explained ”طَيِّبٌ حُجُزاتُهُمْ“ as meaning that they are chaste. Likewise ﴿فَنَفَخْنا فِيهِ مِن رُوحِنا﴾ means: into the opening of her garment.
